title.zh: 卷二百四十九 列傳第八 范質 王溥 魏仁浦
title.en: Volume 249 Biographies 8: Fan Zhi, Wang Pu, Wei Renpu
title.raw: 卷二百四十九 列傳第八 范質 王溥 魏仁浦 Volume 249 Biographies 8: Fan Zhi, Wang Pu, Wei Renpu

sentences.zh: 范質，字文素，大名宗城人。

translations.literal: Fan Zhi, styled Wensu, was a native of Zongcheng in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi, whose style name was Wensu, came from Zongcheng in Daming.

sentences.zh: 父守遇，鄭州防禦判官。

translations.literal: His father Shouyu was a legal adviser in the Zhengzhou defense command.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Shouyu, served as legal adviser to the Zhengzhou defense command.

sentences.zh: 質生之夕，母夢神人授以五色筆。

translations.literal: On the night Zhi was born, his mother dreamed that a divine being gave her a five-colored brush.
translations.idiomatic: The night he was born, his mother dreamed that a god handed her a brush in five colors.

sentences.zh: 九歲能屬文，十三治《尚書》，教授生徒。

translations.literal: At nine he could compose essays; at thirteen he mastered the Book of Documents and taught students.
translations.idiomatic: He could write prose at nine, and at thirteen he had mastered the Book of Documents and was teaching pupils.

sentences.zh: 後唐長興四年，舉進士，為忠武軍節度推官，遷封丘令。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing of Later Tang, he passed the jinshi examination, became a staff officer under the Zhongwu military commissioner, and was promoted to magistrate of Fengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In 933 he passed the jinshi examination, served as staff officer to the Zhongwu commissioner, and was later appointed magistrate of Fengqiu.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，以文章干宰相桑維翰，深器之，即奏為監察御史。

translations.literal: During the Tianfu era of Jin, he presented his writings to the chief minister Sang Weihan, who greatly valued him and immediately memorialized to appoint him investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianfu period he sought out Chief Minister Sang Weihan with his literary work; Sang was deeply impressed and had him appointed investigating censor at once.

sentences.zh: 及維翰出鎮相州，歷泰寧、晉昌二節度，皆請質為從事。

translations.literal: When Weihan went out to govern Xiangzhou and successively held the Taining and Jinchang commissions, he each time requested Zhi as his staff member.
translations.idiomatic: When Weihan left the capital to govern Xiangzhou and later held the Taining and Jinchang commands in turn, he asked to have Zhi on his staff each time.

sentences.zh: 維翰再相，質遷主客員外郎、直史館。

translations.literal: When Weihan became chief minister again, Zhi was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Receptions and compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Weihan returned as chief minister, Zhi was made vice director of the Bureau of Receptions and a compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，召入為翰林學士，加比部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned in as Hanlin academician, with the additional titles of director in the Bureau of Reviews and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was called to court as a Hanlin academician, with concurrent appointment as director in the Bureau of Reviews and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 契丹侵邊，少帝命漢祖等十五將出征。

translations.literal: When the Khitans invaded the frontier, the Young Emperor ordered Liu Zhiyuan and fourteen other generals to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans raided the border, Emperor Chu ordered Liu Zhiyuan and fourteen other commanders to take the field.

sentences.zh: 是夜，質入直，少帝令召諸學士分草制，質曰：「宮城已閉，恐泄機事。」

translations.literal: That night Zhi was on duty in the palace; the Young Emperor ordered the academicians summoned to draft edicts separately, but Zhi said, "The palace gates are already closed—there is fear of leaking confidential matters."
translations.idiomatic: That night, while on palace duty, he was told to summon the other academicians to divide the drafting work. Zhi objected: "The palace gates are shut; we might leak state secrets."

sentences.zh: 獨具草以進，辭理優贍，當時稱之。

translations.literal: He alone prepared the draft and submitted it; its language and reasoning were excellent and ample, and he was praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the entire set of documents himself. The prose was polished and ample, and contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 漢初，加中書舍人、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he was additionally appointed Secretariat drafter and vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han was founded, he was also made Secretariat drafter and vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 周祖征叛，每朝廷遣使賫詔處分軍事，皆合機宜。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder campaigned against rebels, whenever the court sent envoys bearing edicts to direct military affairs, they all fit the strategic moment.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taizu of Zhou's campaigns against rebellion, every edict the court sent out to direct operations proved apt to the situation.

sentences.zh: 周祖問誰為此辭，使者以質對，歎曰：「宰相器也。」

translations.literal: The Zhou founder asked who had written these words; the envoy named Zhi, and he sighed, "Material for a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder asked who had written them. When the envoy named Zhi, he sighed and said, "This man has the makings of a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 周祖自鄴起兵向闕，京城擾亂，質匿民間，物色得之，喜甚，時大雪，解袍衣之，且令草太后誥及議迎湘陰公儀注，質蒼黃論撰，稱旨，乃白太后，以質為兵部侍郎、樞密副使。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder raised troops from Ye and marched on the capital, the capital was in turmoil; Zhi hid among the populace, was sought out and found, and the founder was greatly pleased. It was snowing heavily; he removed his robe and clothed Zhi in it, and also ordered him to draft the empress dowager's proclamation and the protocol for receiving the Duke of Xiangyin. Zhi, in haste, composed and discussed them; they accorded with the intent, and he reported to the empress dowager, appointing Zhi vice minister of war and deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei marched from Ye on the capital, the city was in chaos and Zhi went into hiding among the people. Once found, Guo Wei was overjoyed. Snow was falling heavily; he took off his own robe and put it on Zhi, then ordered him to draft the empress dowager's proclamation and the protocol for welcoming the Duke of Xiangyin. Zhi worked in frantic haste; his drafts pleased the founder, who then told the empress dowager to appoint Zhi vice minister of war and deputy military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，加拜中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun of Zhou he was further appointed vice director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangshun era he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 翌日，兼參知樞密院事。

translations.literal: The next day he was additionally made participant in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he was also made a participant in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 郊祀畢，進位左僕射兼門下侍郎、平章事、監修國史。

translations.literal: After the suburban sacrifice was completed, he was advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent appointment as vice director of the Chancellery, Grand Councilor, and supervisor of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban sacrifice he was promoted to Left Vice Director of State Affairs, with concurrent posts as vice director of the Chancellery, Grand Councilor, and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 從征高平還，加司徒、弘文館大學士。

translations.literal: Returning from the campaign at Gaoping, he was given the additional titles of Minister of Education and grand academician of the Hall for the Advancement of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from the Gaoping campaign he was made Minister of Education and grand academician of the Hall for the Advancement of Literature.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年夏，從征壽州還，加爵邑。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of Xiande, returning from the campaign against Shouzhou, he received additional noble rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 957, after the Shouzhou campaign, his noble rank and fief were increased.

sentences.zh: 質建議以律條繁冗，輕重無據，吏得因緣為奸。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized that the legal articles were prolix and redundant, that severity and leniency had no fixed basis, and that clerks could exploit openings to commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi argued that the statutes had grown bloated, that penalties lacked clear standards, and that clerks were free to twist the law for private gain.

sentences.zh: 世宗特命詳定，是為《刑統》。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong specially ordered a detailed revision, and this became the Penal Code Compendium.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong ordered a full revision, producing the Penal Code Compendium.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，世宗北征，質病留京師，賜錢百萬，俾市醫藥。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year, when Emperor Shizong campaigned north, Zhi was ill and remained in the capital; he was granted a million in cash to buy medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of his sixth year on the throne, Shizong marched north while Zhi, ill, stayed in the capital and was given a million cash to buy medicine.

sentences.zh: 及平關南，至瀛州，質見於路左。

translations.literal: When the Guannan region was pacified and the army reached Yingzhou, Zhi was seen by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: After Guannan was pacified, the army reached Yingzhou and found Zhi waiting by the road.

sentences.zh: 師還，以樞密使魏仁浦為相，命質與王溥並參知樞密院事。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Wei Renpu, military affairs commissioner, was made chief minister; Zhi and Wang Pu were both ordered to participate in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, Wei Renpu was made chief minister while Zhi and Wang Pu were both appointed participants in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 世宗不豫，入受顧命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong fell ill, he entered to receive the dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong fell gravely ill, Zhi was summoned to receive his final charge.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，加開府儀同三司，封蕭國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Zhi was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor with the ceremonial privileges of a three-office opening, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Zhi was made Grand Preceptor with third-rank opening privileges and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 及太祖北征，為六師推載，自陳橋還府署。

translations.literal: When the Taizu campaigned north, the six armies pressed the yellow robe on him; he returned from Chenqiao to his official residence.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizu's northern campaign the army forced the imperial mantle on him at Chenqiao, and he returned to his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時質方就食閣中，太祖入，率王溥、魏仁浦就府謁見。

translations.literal: At that time Zhi was just taking a meal in the pavilion; Taizu entered, leading Wang Pu and Wei Renpu to the residence to pay their respects.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was at dinner in his pavilion when Taizu arrived with Wang Pu and Wei Renpu to pay their respects at his residence.

sentences.zh: 太祖對之嗚咽流涕，具言擁逼之狀。

translations.literal: Taizu faced them sobbing and shedding tears, fully explaining how he had been coerced.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu wept before them and described in full how the troops had forced his hand.

sentences.zh: 質等未及對，軍校羅彥瓌舉刃擬質曰：「我輩無主，今日須得天子。」

translations.literal: Before Zhi and the others could reply, the army officer Luo Yanqiong raised his blade toward Zhi and said, "We have no lord; today we must have an emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Before they could answer, the officer Luo Yanqiong leveled his blade at Zhi and said, "We have no ruler—we must have an emperor today."

sentences.zh: 太祖叱彥瓌不退，質不知所措，乃與溥等降階受命。

translations.literal: Taizu rebuked Yanqiong but he would not withdraw; Zhi did not know what to do, and thereupon he and Pu and the others descended the steps to accept the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu shouted at Yanqiong, but the man would not stand down. At a loss, Zhi went down the steps with Pu and the others to accept the mandate.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加兼侍中，罷參知樞密。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was additionally made concurrent Palace Attendant and removed from participating in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was additionally made Palace Attendant and relieved of his military affairs duties.

sentences.zh: 俄被疾，太祖征澤、潞，幸其第，賜黃金器二百兩、銀器千兩、絹二千匹、錢二百萬。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill; when Taizu campaigned against Ze and Lu, he visited his residence and bestowed two hundred taels of gold vessels, one thousand taels of silver vessels, two thousand bolts of silk, and two million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he fell ill. When Taizu campaigned against Ze and Lu, he visited Zhi's home and gave him two hundred taels of gold vessels, one thousand taels of silver, two thousand bolts of silk, and two million cash.

sentences.zh: 太祖初即位，庶事謙抑，至於藩戚尚未崇建幕府，賓佐未列於位。

translations.literal: When Taizu first acceded, in all matters he was modest and restrained; as for imperial kin, he had not yet greatly established staff offices, and advisers were not yet seated in formal posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu first took the throne he was modest in all matters. He had not yet established formal staff offices for imperial kin, and their advisers had not been given court seats.

sentences.zh: 質因上奏曰：「自古帝王開基創業，封建子弟，樹立磐維，宗戚既隆，社稷永固。

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon memorialized, saying, "From antiquity emperors who founded states and began enterprises enfeoffed their sons and younger brothers and set up firm supports; when imperial kin are exalted, the altars of state are forever secure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized: "Since antiquity, founding emperors have enfeoffed sons and brothers to secure the throne.

sentences.zh: 伏見皇弟泰寧軍節度使光義，自居戎職，特負將材，及領藩維，尤積時望；

translations.literal: I humbly observe that the imperial younger brother Guangyi, military commissioner of Taining, since taking military office has borne special talent as a commander, and in leading a regional command has especially accumulated timely renown;
translations.idiomatic: Your younger brother Guangyi, military commissioner of Taining, has shown command talent since taking military office and has won wide respect in his regional post;

sentences.zh: 嘉州防禦使光美，雄俊老成，修身樂善，嘉譽日聞。

translations.literal: Guangmei, defense commissioner of Jiazhou, is bold, handsome, mature, cultivates himself and delights in goodness, and his fine reputation grows daily.
translations.idiomatic: Guangmei, defense commissioner of Jiazhou, is bold, mature, and widely praised for his conduct.

sentences.zh: 乞並行封冊，申錫命書。

translations.literal: I beg that enfeoffments and investitures be carried out together and edicts of appointment be granted.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that both receive enfeoffment and appointment edicts.

sentences.zh: 皇子皇女雖在繈褓者，亦乞下有司許行恩制，此臣之願也。

translations.literal: Even princes and princesses still in swaddling clothes, I beg that the relevant offices be ordered to allow the bestowal of grace decrees—this is my wish.
translations.idiomatic: Even infant princes and princesses should receive grace decrees through the proper offices—that is my wish.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞為宰相者，當舉賢能，以輔佐天子。

translations.literal: I have also heard that one who serves as chief minister should recommend the worthy and able to assist the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I also believe a chief minister should recommend the worthy to assist the throne.

sentences.zh: 竊以端明殿學士呂餘慶、樞密副使趙普精通治道，經事霸府，歷歲滋深，睹其公忠，誠堪毗倚。

translations.literal: I venture that Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity Lu Yuqing and Deputy Military Affairs Commissioner Zhao Pu are thoroughly versed in the art of governance, have served the founding lord's headquarters, and over the years have grown ever deeper in experience; seeing their public loyalty, they are truly fit to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuqing, academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity, and Zhao Pu, deputy military affairs commissioner, are deeply versed in governance, long tested in the founding lord's service, and plainly loyal.

sentences.zh: 乞授以臺司，俾申才用。」

translations.literal: I beg that they be granted posts in the central ministries so their talents may be put to use."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that they be given central ministry posts so their talents may be used."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 先是，宰相見天子議大政事，必命坐面議之，從容賜茶而退，唐及五代猶遵此制。

translations.literal: Previously, when chief ministers saw the Son of Heaven to discuss great affairs of state, they were always ordered to be seated and discuss face to face, were unhurriedly granted tea and then withdrew; Tang and the Five Dynasties still followed this institution.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when chief ministers met the emperor on major policy, they were seated to discuss matters face to face, offered tea at leisure, and then dismissed—a custom Tang and the Five Dynasties had kept.

sentences.zh: 及質等憚帝英睿，每事輒具劄子進呈，具言曰：「如此庶盡稟承之方，免妄庸之失。」

translations.literal: When Zhi and the others feared the emperor's keen intelligence, on every matter they would prepare memorials and submit them, stating in full, "In this way we may exhaust the methods of receiving and carrying out orders, and avoid reckless and mediocre errors."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the emperor's sharp mind, Zhi and his colleagues began submitting written memorials on every issue, stating, "In this way we may exhaust the methods of receiving and carrying out orders and avoid reckless and mediocre errors."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 由是奏御寖多，始廢坐論之禮。

translations.literal: From this memorials to the throne gradually increased, and the seated discussion rite was first abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Written memorials multiplied, and the seated council with the emperor was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，帝將有事圜丘，以質為大禮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande the emperor was about to perform the suburban sacrifice at the Round Mound; he appointed Zhi chief ritual commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiande era, when the emperor prepared to offer at the Round Mound, he made Zhi chief ritual commissioner.

sentences.zh: 質與鹵簿使張昭、儀仗使劉溫叟討論舊典，定《南郊行禮圖》上之。

translations.literal: Zhi, together with Zhang Zhao, commissioner of the honor guard, and Liu Wensou, commissioner of ceremonial regalia, discussed the old canons and fixed the Diagram of Rites for the Southern Suburban Sacrifice, which they submitted.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Zhao, commissioner of the honor guard, and Liu Wensou, commissioner of ceremonial regalia, Zhi reviewed ancient precedents and submitted the Diagram of Rites for the Southern Suburban Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 帝尤嘉獎。

translations.literal: The emperor especially praised and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was especially pleased and rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 由是禮文始備，質自為序。

translations.literal: From this ritual texts began to be complete, and Zhi himself wrote the preface.
translations.idiomatic: Court ritual was thereby put on a proper footing, and Zhi wrote the preface himself.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，進封魯國公，質奉表固辭，不允。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu; Zhi submitted a memorial firmly declining, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: After the ceremony he was promoted to Duke of Lu. Zhi memorialized to decline, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，罷為太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year he was removed and made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 964 he was relieved of office and made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 九月，卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 將終，戒其子旻勿請謚，勿刻墓碑。

translations.literal: As he was about to die, he admonished his son Min not to request a posthumous title and not to carve a tomb stele.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his son Min not to seek a posthumous title or erect a tomb inscription.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之為悲惋，罷朝。

translations.literal: When Taizu heard of it he was grieved and regretful and dismissed court.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was deeply grieved when he heard the news and canceled court for the day.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令，賜絹五百匹、粟麥各百石。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Director of the Secretariat and granted five hundred bolts of silk and a hundred piculs each of grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat, with gifts of five hundred bolts of silk and a hundred piculs each of grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 質力學強記，性明悟。

translations.literal: Zhi exerted himself in learning and had a powerful memory; by nature he was clear and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was a tireless scholar with an exceptional memory and a keen, perceptive mind.

sentences.zh: 舉進士時，和凝以翰林學士典貢部，覽質所試文字，重之，自以登第名在十三，亦以其數處之。

translations.literal: When he took the jinshi examination, He Ning, as Hanlin academician, presided over the examinations department; reading Zhi's examination compositions, he valued them highly. He himself had passed the examination ranked thirteenth, and he also placed Zhi at that number.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi sat for the jinshi examination, He Ning of the Hanlin Academy presided over the board. Impressed by Zhi's papers—and mindful that he himself had placed thirteenth on the list—He ranked Zhi thirteenth as well.

sentences.zh: 貢闈中謂之「傳衣缽」。

translations.literal: In the examination compound this was called "passing on the robe and bowl."
translations.idiomatic: Candidates called this "passing on the robe and bowl"—the transmission of a master's legacy.

sentences.zh: 其後質登相位，為太子太傅，封魯國公，皆與凝同云。

translations.literal: Later when Zhi reached the chief minister's position, became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, all were the same as Ning's.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhi rose to chief minister, became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and was enfeoffed Duke of Lu, each milestone matched He's own career.

sentences.zh: 初，質既登朝，猶手不釋卷，人或勞之，質曰：「有善相者，謂我異日位宰輔，誠如其言，不學何術以處之？」

translations.literal: At first, after Zhi had entered court service, he still never put down his books in hand; some urged him to rest, and Zhi said, "There was a skilled physiognomist who said I would one day stand as chief minister. If that is truly so, by what art could I hold such a post without study?"
translations.idiomatic: Even after he entered government service he never stopped reading. When others urged him to rest, he said, "A fortune-teller once told me I would reach the highest office. If he was right, what skill could carry me there without study?"

sentences.zh: 後從世宗征淮南，詔令多出其手，吳中文士莫不驚伏。

translations.literal: Later, following Emperor Shizong's campaign against Huainan, many edicts and orders came from his hand, and the literary men of Wu were all startled into submission.
translations.idiomatic: On Shizong's Huainan campaign, many of the emperor's edicts came from his pen, and the literati of Wu were left in awe.

sentences.zh: 質每下制敕，未嘗破律，命刺史縣令，必以戶口版籍為急。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhi issued edicts and orders, he never violated the statutes; in appointing prefects and magistrates he always made household registers and census records urgent priorities.
translations.idiomatic: His edicts never bent the law, and in appointing prefects and magistrates he always stressed household registers and tax rolls as top priorities.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使視民田，按獄訟，皆延見，為述天子憂勤之意，然後遣之。

translations.literal: Whenever the court sent envoys to inspect the people's fields or investigate lawsuits, he always received them in audience, explained the Son of Heaven's anxious diligence on their behalf, and only then sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court dispatched envoys to inspect farmland or review lawsuits, he received them personally, explained the emperor's tireless concern for the people, and only then sent them on their way.

sentences.zh: 世宗初征淮南，駐壽、濠，銳意攻取，且議行幸揚州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong first campaigned against Huainan, he halted at Shou and Hao, was intent on storming and taking, and also discussed proceeding in person to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On Shizong's first Huainan campaign he halted at Shou and Hao, pressed hard for a decisive assault, and even discussed visiting Yangzhou in person.

sentences.zh: 質以師老，與王溥泣諫乃止。

translations.literal: Zhi, on the grounds that the army was weary, together with Wang Pu wept and remonstrated until the plan was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi argued that the army was exhausted; he and Wang Pu wept in remonstrance until the emperor abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 及再駕揚州，因事怒竇儀，罪在不測，質入謁請見，世宗意其救儀，起避之，質趨前曰：「儀近臣也，過小不當誅。」

translations.literal: When he again proceeded to Yangzhou, he grew angry over a matter with Dou Yi; the offense was beyond prediction. Zhi entered to request an audience; Emperor Shizong supposed he had come to save Yi and rose to avoid him. Zhi hurried forward and said, "Yi is a close minister; the fault is small and he ought not to be executed."
translations.idiomatic: On a later visit to Yangzhou the emperor flew into a rage over Dou Yi, whose punishment seemed uncertain. Zhi asked for an audience; Shizong assumed he had come to plead for Yi and rose to avoid him. Zhi stepped forward and said, "Yi is a close adviser—the offense is slight and does not warrant death."

sentences.zh: 因免冠叩頭泣下，曰：「臣備位宰相，豈可使人主暴怒，致近臣於死地耶？

translations.literal: He thereupon removed his cap and kowtowed, weeping, and said, "Your servant holds a chief minister's post in name only—how could I let the sovereign fly into violent anger and bring a close minister to the gate of death?
translations.idiomatic: He removed his cap, kowtowed, and wept. "I hold the title of chief minister in name only—how can I stand by while my lord's wrath sends a close adviser to his death?

sentences.zh: 願寬儀罪。」

translations.literal: I beg that Yi's offense be leniently treated."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to show Yi mercy."

sentences.zh: 世宗意遂解，復坐，即遣赦儀。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong's mind was then eased; he sat again and immediately sent to pardon Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong's anger lifted. He sat down again and at once ordered Yi's pardon.

sentences.zh: 質性卞急，好面折人。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was stern and impatient; he liked to rebuke people to their faces.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and impatient by nature and prone to blunt rebukes.

sentences.zh: 以廉介自持，未嘗受四方饋遺，前後所得祿賜多給孤遺。

translations.literal: He maintained himself with integrity and uprightness, never accepted gifts from the four directions, and gave most of his salaries and rewards over the years to orphans and the bereaved.
translations.idiomatic: He held himself to strict integrity, never accepted gifts from any quarter, and gave most of his salary and imperial rewards to orphans and the destitute.

sentences.zh: 閨門之中，食不異品。

translations.literal: Within his household, food was not of different grades.
translations.idiomatic: Within his household everyone ate the same fare—no special dishes for himself.

sentences.zh: 身沒，家無餘貲。

translations.literal: When his person perished, the family had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his family had nothing left in reserve.

sentences.zh: 太祖因論輔相，謂侍臣曰：「朕聞范質止有居第，不事生產，真宰相也。」

translations.literal: Taizu, while discussing chief ministers, said to his attending officials, "I have heard that Fan Zhi has only a residence and does not engage in production—truly a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Discussing chief ministers one day, Taizu told his attendants, "I hear Fan Zhi owns only his house and does not pursue profit—a true chief minister."

sentences.zh: 太宗亦嘗稱之曰：「宰輔中能循規矩、慎名器、持廉節，無出質右者，但欠世宗一死，為可惜爾。」

translations.literal: Taizong also once praised him, saying, "Among chief ministers, none surpasses Zhi in following rules and measures, being careful with titles and offices, and maintaining integrity—only he lacked dying for Emperor Shizong, which is a pity."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once said of him, "Among chief ministers, none better observed rules, guarded titles and offices, and kept his integrity—but he failed to die for Shizong, which is regrettable."

sentences.zh: 從子校書郎杲求奏遷秩，質作詩曉之，時人傳誦以為勸戒。

translations.literal: His nephew, the collator Gao, requested a memorial for promotion in rank; Zhi composed a poem to enlighten him, and people of the time transmitted and recited it as admonition.
translations.idiomatic: When his nephew Gao, a collator in the palace library, asked him to seek a promotion, Zhi wrote a poem of admonition that contemporaries widely quoted as a moral lesson.

sentences.zh: 有集三十卷，又述朱梁至周五代為《通錄》六十五卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty scrolls, and also narrated from Later Liang through the Five Dynasties period in the Comprehensive Record in sixty-five scrolls, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in thirty scrolls and a sixty-five-scroll Comprehensive Record covering Later Liang through the Five Dynasties, both widely circulated.

sentences.zh: 子旻。

translations.literal: His son was Min.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Min.

sentences.zh: 子 旻

translations.literal: Son: Min
translations.idiomatic: Son: Min

sentences.zh: 旻，字貴參，十歲能屬文。

translations.literal: Min, styled Guican, at ten could compose essays.
translations.idiomatic: Min, whose style name was Guican, could write prose at the age of ten.

sentences.zh: 以父任右千牛備身、太子司議郎，累遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: By his father's privilege he was made Right Corps Cadet of the Thousand Oxen and Remonstrance Secretary of the Heir Apparent, and was repeatedly promoted to assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege he entered service as Right Corps Cadet of the Thousand Oxen and Remonstrance Secretary of the Heir Apparent, and rose eventually to assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 宋初，為度支員外郎、判大理正事，俄知開封縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was vice director in the Bureau of Revenue and concurrently judged chief cases in the Court of Judicial Review; soon he was made magistrate of Kaifeng county.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he served as vice director in the Bureau of Revenue and judge of chief cases in the Court of Judicial Review, and soon became magistrate of Kaifeng county.

sentences.zh: 太宗時領京尹，數召與語，頗器重之。

translations.literal: When Taizong held the capital intendancy, he repeatedly summoned Min to converse with him and greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong served as capital intendant he often summoned Min for conversation and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 嶺南平，遷知邕州兼水陸轉運使。

translations.literal: When Lingnan was pacified, he was transferred to govern Yongzhou with concurrent appointment as commissioner for land and water transport.
translations.idiomatic: After Lingnan was pacified he was appointed prefect of Yongzhou and commissioner for land and water transport.

sentences.zh: 俗好淫祀，輕醫藥，重鬼神，旻下令禁之。

translations.literal: The custom favored licentious sacrifices, slighted medicine, and valued ghosts and spirits; Min issued orders forbidding this.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom favored improper sacrifices, neglected medicine, and trusted spirits; Min banned such practices by order.

sentences.zh: 且割己奉市藥以給病者，愈者千計，復以方書刻石置廳壁，民感化之。

translations.literal: Moreover he cut his own salary to buy medicine in the market for the sick; those cured numbered in the thousands. He also had medical formulas carved in stone and set on the hall walls, and the people were moved and transformed.
translations.idiomatic: He cut his own salary to buy medicine for the sick; thousands recovered. He had medical formulas carved on stone tablets in the government hall, and the people were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 會南漢知廣州官鄧存忠劫土人二萬眾，攻州城七十餘日。

translations.literal: It happened that Deng Cunzhong, an official of Southern Han who knew Guangzhou, seized twenty thousand local people and attacked the prefectural city for more than seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Cunzhong, a former Southern Han official in Guangzhou, then rallied twenty thousand locals and besieged the prefectural city for more than seventy days.

sentences.zh: 旻屢出親戰，矢集於胸，猶激勵將卒殊死戰，賊遂少卻，病創日篤，堅壁固守，遣使十五輩求援。

translations.literal: Min repeatedly went out to fight in person; arrows clustered on his chest, yet he still roused officers and soldiers to fight to the death. The bandits then somewhat withdrew. His wound illness grew daily severe; he firmly walled the city and held fast, and sent fifteen envoys to seek relief.
translations.idiomatic: Min repeatedly led the fight in person. Arrows struck his chest, yet he still roused his men to battle to the death until the rebels drew back somewhat. As his wound worsened he held the walls and sent fifteen separate missions to request reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 廣州救兵至，圍解，賜璽書獎之。

translations.literal: When Guangzhou relief troops arrived, the siege was lifted, and an imperial sealed letter was granted to commend him.
translations.idiomatic: When relief forces from Guangzhou arrived the siege was lifted, and the court sent a sealed commendation.

sentences.zh: 旻病甚，詔令有司以肩輿載歸闕下。

translations.literal: When Min's illness was severe, an edict ordered the relevant offices to carry him back to the capital in a sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave, an edict ordered officials to bring him back to the capital in a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 疾愈，通判鎮州，有能聲，賜錢二百萬，遷庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: When his illness recovered, he was made vice prefect of Zhenzhou, gained a reputation for ability, was granted two million in cash, and was promoted to vice director in the Bureau of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: After he recovered he served as vice prefect of Zhenzhou, earned a reputation for competence, received two million cash, and was promoted to vice director in the Bureau of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 開寶九年，知淮南轉運事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaibao he was put in charge of Huainan transport affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 976 he was placed in charge of transport for Huainan.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂旻曰：「朕今委卿以方面之重，凡除民隱、急軍須之務，悉以便宜從事，無庸一一中覆也。」

translations.literal: Taizu said to Min, "I now entrust you with the heavy responsibility of a frontier region. In all matters of removing the people's hidden grievances and urgently supplying military needs, you may entirely act as expedient without needing to report each one for approval."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told him, "I now entrust you with a frontier command. On relieving the people's burdens and meeting urgent military needs, act at your own discretion—there is no need to report every decision for approval."

sentences.zh: 歲運米百餘萬石給京師，當時稱有心計。

translations.literal: Each year he transported more than a million piculs of rice to supply the capital, and he was at the time praised as having a calculating mind.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he shipped more than a million piculs of grain to the capital, and contemporaries praised his resourcefulness.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，召為水部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was summoned as director in the Bureau of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he was recalled as director in the Bureau of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 錢俶獻地，以旻為考功郎中，權知兩浙諸州軍事。

translations.literal: When Qian Chu surrendered his territory, Min was made director in the Bureau of Evaluations and given provisional authority over the military affairs of the various prefectures of the two Zhe regions.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Chu surrendered his domain, Min was made director in the Bureau of Evaluations with provisional authority over military affairs in the two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 旻上言：「俶在國日，徭賦繁苛，凡薪粒、蔬果、箕帚之屬悉收算。

translations.literal: Min memorialized, "In the days when Chu held his state, corvée and taxes were numerous and harsh; everything from firewood and grain to fruits, vegetables, and brooms was all subject to levies.
translations.idiomatic: Min memorialized: "While Qian Chu still ruled, taxes were crushing—even firewood, grain, fruit, vegetables, and brooms were all assessed.

sentences.zh: 欲盡釋不取，以蠲其弊。」

translations.literal: I wish to release all of these entirely and not collect them, in order to remit these abuses."
translations.idiomatic: I propose to abolish these levies entirely and lift the burden on the people."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 車駕征晉陽，上書求從，召為右諫議大夫、三司副使，判行在三司，又兼吏部選事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned against Jinyang, he submitted a memorial requesting to follow; he was summoned as Right Remonstrance Grandee, vice commissioner of the Three Departments, with concurrent judgment of the traveling Three Departments, and also concurrently handled selection affairs in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Jinyang, Min asked to accompany the army and was made Right Remonstrance Grandee and vice commissioner of the Three Departments, with charge of the traveling Three Departments and concurrent responsibility for personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 師還，加給事中。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was given the additional title of Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned he was made Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 坐受人請求擅市竹木入官，為王仁贍所發，貶房州司戶。

translations.literal: He was punished for accepting others' requests and on his own authority purchasing bamboo and timber for the government; he was exposed by Wang Renshan and demoted to registrar of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted of accepting favors and improperly purchasing bamboo and timber for the government on his own authority. Exposed by Wang Renshan, he was demoted to registrar of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 語在 《仁贍傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the Biography of Renshan.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Wang Renshan.

sentences.zh: 量移唐州。

translations.literal: He was transferred by degree to Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷、《邕管記》三卷。

translations.literal: He had collected works in twenty scrolls and Records of Yong and Guan in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty scrolls and Records of Yong and Guan in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 其後，子貽孫上言，詔復舊官。

translations.literal: Later his son Yisun submitted a memorial, and an edict restored his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Later his son Yisun petitioned the throne, and an edict restored Min's former rank.

sentences.zh: 貽孫官至主客員外郎。

translations.literal: Yisun reached the office of vice director in the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun rose to vice director in the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 兄子 杲

translations.literal: Nephew: Gao
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Gao

sentences.zh: 杲，字師回，父正，青州從事。

translations.literal: Gao, styled Shihui, had a father Zheng who was a staff member in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, whose style name was Shihui, was the son of Zheng, a Qingzhou staff officer.

sentences.zh: 杲少孤，質視如己子。

translations.literal: Gao was orphaned young; Zhi treated him as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, Gao was raised by his uncle Zhi as though he were his own son.

sentences.zh: 刻志於學，與姑臧李均、汾陽郭昱齊名，為文深僻難曉，後生多慕效之。

translations.literal: He devoted himself zealously to study, was equally famous with Li Jun of Guzang and Guo Yu of Fenyang, and his writing was abstruse and hard to understand; many younger men admired and imitated him.
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself rigorously to learning and was ranked with Li Jun of Guzang and Guo Yu of Fenyang. His prose was deliberately obscure, and many younger writers imitated his style.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補太廟齋郎，再遷國子四門博士。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he was made Acolyte of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and was later promoted to Four Gates Doctor in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered service as an acolyte of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was later promoted to Four Gates Doctor in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 嘗攜文謁陶穀、竇儀，咸大稱賞，謂杲曰：「若舉進士，當待汝以甲科。」

translations.literal: He once brought his writings to visit Tao Gu and Dou Yi; both greatly praised and rewarded him, saying to Gao, "If you take the jinshi examination, you should be placed in the top class."
translations.idiomatic: He once showed his writings to Tao Gu and Dou Yi, who praised them highly and told him, "If you sit for the jinshi examination, you should rank in the top class."

sentences.zh: 及秋試，有上書言閥閱之家不當與寒士爭科第，杲遂不應舉。

translations.literal: When the autumn examination came, someone submitted a memorial saying that families of distinguished pedigree ought not compete for degrees with poor scholars; Gao thereupon did not answer the examination.
translations.idiomatic: When the autumn examination arrived, a memorial argued that men of eminent families should not compete with poor scholars for degrees. Gao declined to sit for the examination.

sentences.zh: 稍遷著作佐郎，出為許、鄧二州從事，坐事免。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to assistant compiler, went out as staff member in the two prefectures of Xu and Deng, and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant compiler, then served on the staffs of Xu and Deng prefectures before being dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，遷著作郎、直史館，歷右拾遺、左補闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to compiler and compiler in the Historiography Institute, and passed through the offices of Right Remembrancer and Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he became a compiler and was assigned to the Historiography Institute, later serving as Right Remembrancer and Left Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，同知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was made associate commissioner of the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In 985 he served as associate commissioner of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 俄上書自言其才比東方朔，求顯用，以觀其效。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted a memorial claiming his talent matched Dongfang Shuo, requesting conspicuous employment to show his effect.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized that his talent rivaled Dongfang Shuo's and asked for a prominent post to prove his worth.

sentences.zh: 太宗壯之，擢知制誥。

translations.literal: Taizong was impressed by his spirit and promoted him to drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was impressed and made him a drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 杲家貧，貸人錢數百萬。

translations.literal: Gao's family was poor; he borrowed several million in cash from others.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's family was poor, and he owed creditors several million cash.

sentences.zh: 母兄晞性嗇，嘗為興元少尹，居京兆，殖貨鉅萬。

translations.literal: His mother's elder brother Xi was stingy by nature; he had once been Vice Intendant of Xingyuan, lived in Jingzhao, and amassed goods worth tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal uncle Xi was miserly by nature. A former vice intendant of Xingyuan, he lived in the capital region and had amassed a fortune of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 親故有自長安來者，紿杲曰：「少尹不復靳財物，已揮金無算矣。」

translations.literal: A relative or friend who had come from Chang'an deceived Gao, saying, "The Vice Intendant no longer begrudges wealth and has already spent gold beyond counting."
translations.idiomatic: A relative arriving from Chang'an deceived him, saying, "Your uncle no longer hoards his wealth—he has been spending gold without limit."

sentences.zh: 杲聞之喜，因上言兄老，求典京兆以便養。

translations.literal: When Gao heard this he was pleased, and thereupon memorialized that his elder brother was old, requesting to govern Jingzhao in order to support him conveniently.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted by this news, Gao memorialized that his elder brother was aged and asked to govern the capital region so he could care for him.

sentences.zh: 太宗從其請。

translations.literal: Taizong followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong granted the request.

sentences.zh: 改工部郎中，罷知制誥。

translations.literal: He was changed to director in the Bureau of Works and removed from drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director in the Bureau of Works and relieved of his edict-drafting duties.

sentences.zh: 杲既至，而晞吝如故，且常以不法事干公府。

translations.literal: After Gao arrived, Xi was stingy as before, and moreover often involved the government offices in unlawful matters.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gao arrived, Xi proved as miserly as ever and frequently embroiled the government in improper affairs.

sentences.zh: 杲大悔。

translations.literal: Gao deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao deeply regretted his decision.

sentences.zh: 杲視事逾年，境內不治。

translations.literal: After Gao had held office for more than a year, the territory within his jurisdiction was not well governed.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year in office, he had failed to bring the region under effective control.

sentences.zh: 會賊帥劉渥剽掠屬縣，吏卒解散，遂驚悸成疾。

translations.literal: It happened that the bandit chief Liu Wo plundered the subordinate counties; clerks and soldiers dispersed, and he thereupon fell ill from fright and palpitation.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit leader Liu Wo raided the subordinate counties, his officers and soldiers scattered. Gao fell ill from shock and anxiety.

sentences.zh: 移知壽州，上言：「家世史官，願秉直筆，成國朝大典。」

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Shouzhou and memorialized, "My family for generations has been historians; I wish to wield the straight brush and complete the great canon of our dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shouzhou, he memorialized: "My family has produced historians for generations. I wish to wield an honest brush and help complete the great chronicle of our dynasty."

sentences.zh: 召為史館修撰，固求掌誥詞，帝從之。

translations.literal: He was summoned as compiler in the Historiography Institute, firmly requested charge of edict drafting, and the emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as a historiography compiler and pressed to be put in charge of edict drafting; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時翰林學士宋白左遷鄜州，賈黃中、李沆參知政事，蘇易簡轉承旨，杲連致書相府，求為學士，且言於宰相李昉曰：「先公嘗授以制誥一編，謂杲才堪此職。」

translations.literal: At that time Hanlin academician Song Bai was demoted to Fuzhou; Jia Huangzhong and Li Hang participated in government affairs; Su Yijian was transferred to chief academician. Gao repeatedly sent letters to the chief minister's office requesting to be made academician, and also said to Chief Minister Li Fang, "My late uncle once handed me a volume of edict drafts, saying Gao's talent was fit for this office."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Song Bai had been demoted from the Hanlin Academy, while Jia Huangzhong and Li Hang served as participants in government and Su Yijian had become chief academician. Gao repeatedly wrote to the chief minister's office seeking a Hanlin post and told Li Fang, "My late uncle once gave me a volume of edict drafts and said my talent suited this office."

sentences.zh: 因出示昉，昉屢開解之。

translations.literal: He thereupon showed it to Fang, and Fang repeatedly explained and dissuaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He showed the volume to Fang, who repeatedly tried to dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，太宗飛白書「玉堂」額以賜翰林，杲又上《玉堂記》，因請備職。

translations.literal: Before long Taizong wrote the plaque "Jade Hall" in flying-white script to bestow on the Hanlin Academy; Gao again submitted the Record of the Jade Hall and thereby requested a post in the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Taizong wrote the "Jade Hall" plaque in flying-white script for the Hanlin Academy. Gao submitted a Record of the Jade Hall and again asked for a post there.

sentences.zh: 太宗惡其躁競，改右諫議大夫、知濠州，復召為史館修撰。

translations.literal: Taizong disliked his restless ambition and changed him to Right Remonstrance Grandee and prefect of Haozhou, then again summoned him as historiography compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong disliked his restless ambition, made him Right Remonstrance Grandee and prefect of Haozhou, then recalled him as historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗以太祖朝典策未備，乃議召杲。

translations.literal: At first Taizong, because the canonical records of Taizu's reign were not complete, discussed summoning Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Taizong had decided that the historical records of Taizu's reign were incomplete and discussed recalling Gao.

sentences.zh: 杲聞命喜甚，以為將加優擢，晨夜趨進。

translations.literal: When Gao heard the order he was extremely pleased, thinking he would receive special promotion, and hurried forward day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Overjoyed at the summons and expecting a major promotion, he hurried to court day and night.

sentences.zh: 至宋州，遇朗州通判錢熙，杲問以「朝議將任僕何官」，熙言：「重修《太祖實錄》爾。」

translations.literal: When he reached Songzhou he met Qian Xi, vice prefect of Langzhou; Gao asked him, "What office will the court deliberation appoint me to?" Xi said, "To revise the Veritable Records of Taizu, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: At Songzhou he met Qian Xi, vice prefect of Langzhou, and asked what post the court intended for him. Xi replied, "To revise the Veritable Records of Taizu—that is all."

sentences.zh: 杲默然。

translations.literal: Gao was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Gao fell silent.

sentences.zh: 久之，感疾，至京師，旬月卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: After a long while he contracted illness, reached the capital, and died within ten days, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He later fell ill, reached the capital, and died within a month at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 太宗閔之，錄其二子。

translations.literal: Taizong pitied him and enrolled his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong took pity on him and enrolled his two sons in office.

sentences.zh: 杲性虛誕，與人交，好面譽背非，惟與柳開善，更相引重，始終無間。

translations.literal: Gao's nature was vain and boastful; in dealings with others he liked to praise to their faces and speak ill behind their backs. Only with Liu Kai was he on good terms; they repeatedly recommended each other and from beginning to end had no breach.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was vain and boastful, prone to flattery in person and slander behind backs. Only with Liu Kai did he maintain a genuine friendship; they recommended each other throughout their lives without estrangement.

sentences.zh: 不善治生，家益貧，杲端坐終日，不知計所出，人皆笑之。

translations.literal: He was not skilled at managing livelihood; the family grew ever poorer. Gao sat upright all day without knowing what plan to adopt, and everyone laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to manage his household affairs, he grew ever poorer. He would sit upright all day without knowing what to do, and people laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 子坦亦登進士第。

translations.literal: His son Tan also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tan also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 王溥，字齊物，并州祁人。

translations.literal: Wang Pu, styled Qiwu, was a native of Qi in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu, whose style name was Qiwu, came from Qi in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父祚，為郡小吏，有心計，從晉祖入洛，掌鹽鐵案，以母老解職歸。

translations.literal: His father Zuo was a minor clerk in the commandery, shrewd by nature; he followed the Jin founder into Luoyang and managed the salt and iron bureau, then resigned and returned home because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zuo was a minor commandery clerk, shrewd by nature. He followed the Jin founder into Luoyang to manage the salt and iron bureau, then resigned and returned home when his mother grew old.

sentences.zh: 漢祖鎮幷門，統行營兵拒契丹，委祚經度芻粟；

translations.literal: When the Han founder governed Bingmen, he commanded the mobile camp army to resist the Khitans and entrusted Zuo with provisioning fodder and grain;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhiyuan governed Bingmen, he commanded the mobile camp army against the Khitans and entrusted Zuo with provisioning fodder and grain;

sentences.zh: 即位，擢為三司副使。

translations.literal: upon accession he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On accession Liu promoted him to vice commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 歷周為隨州刺史。

translations.literal: Through Zhou he served as prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Zhou he served as prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 漢法禁牛革，輦送京師，遇暑雨多腐壞，祚請班鎧甲之式於諸州，令裁之以輸，民甚便之。

translations.literal: Han law forbade ox hides; they were carted to the capital, and in summer rains many rotted. Zuo requested that patterns for armor be distributed to the prefectures and that hides be cut to measure for delivery; the people found this very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han law forbade the export of ox hides to the capital, and many hides rotted in summer rains on the road. Zuo had armor patterns distributed to the prefectures so hides could be cut locally for delivery, which greatly eased the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 移刺商州，以奉錢募人開大秦山巖梯路，行旅感其惠。

translations.literal: Transferred to govern Shangzhou, he used his salary to hire men to open a ladder road through the cliffs of Mount Daqin; travelers were grateful for his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Shangzhou he used his salary to hire laborers to cut a cliff ladder road through Mount Daqin, to the gratitude of travelers.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，置華州節度，以祚為刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande the Huazhou commission was established and Zuo was made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiande era the Huazhou commission was established and Zuo was appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改鎮潁州，均部內租稅，補實流徙，以出舊籍。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to govern Yingzhou, equalized taxes within the circuit, filled in displaced persons to make registers whole, and removed them from old rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon transferred to Yingzhou, he equalized circuit taxes, restored displaced households to the registers, and cleared outdated rolls.

sentences.zh: 州境舊有通商渠，距淮三百里，歲久湮塞，祚疏導之，遂通舟楫，郡無水患。

translations.literal: Within the prefecture there had been an old Tongshang Canal three hundred li from the Huai; after years it was silted shut. Zuo dredged and opened it, and boats could pass; the commandery had no further flood trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had an old Tongshang Canal three hundred li from the Huai that had silted shut over the years. Zuo dredged it, restored navigation, and ended the commandery's flood troubles.

sentences.zh: 歷鄭州團練使。

translations.literal: He later served as regimentation commissioner of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as regimentation commissioner of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，升宿州為防禦，以祚為使，課民鑿井修火備，築城北堤以禦水災。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, Suzhou was raised to a defense command and Zuo was made commissioner; he set the people to digging wells and preparing fire defenses and built the north dike of the city wall to guard against flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, Suzhou was raised to a defense command with Zuo as commissioner. He had the people dig wells and prepare fire defenses and built the north city dike against floods.

sentences.zh: 因求致政，至闕下，拜左領軍衛上將軍致仕。

translations.literal: He then requested retirement; arriving at court he was appointed honorary Left Leading Army Guard grand general and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He then sought retirement. On reaching court he was made honorary grand general of the Left Leading Army Guard and allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 溥，漢乾祐中，舉進士甲科，為秘書郎。

translations.literal: Pu, during Qianyou of Han, passed the jinshi examination in the top class and was made Secretariat gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou era of Later Han, Pu passed the jinshi examination in the top class and became a Secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時李守貞據河中，趙思綰反京兆，王景崇反鳳翔，周祖將兵討之，辟溥為從事。

translations.literal: At that time Li Shouzhen held Hezhong, Zhao Sijian rebelled in Jingzhao, and Wang Jingchong rebelled in Fengxiang; the Zhou founder led troops to suppress them and recruited Pu as staff member.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shouzhen held Hezhong, Zhao Sijian rebelled in the capital region, and Wang Jingchong rebelled in Fengxiang, Guo Wei marched to suppress them and recruited Pu to his staff.

sentences.zh: 河中平，得賊中文書，多朝貴及藩鎮交結語。

translations.literal: When Hezhong was pacified, documents from within the rebels were obtained; many contained language of collusion with court nobles and military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: After Hezhong fell, captured rebel documents revealed correspondence with many court nobles and military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 周祖籍其名，將按之，溥諫曰：「魑魅之形，伺夜而出，日月既照，氛沴自消。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder recorded their names and was about to investigate; Pu remonstrated, "The forms of goblins and demons wait for night to come forth; once sun and moon have shone, malignant vapors vanish of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei noted the names and prepared to investigate. Pu remonstrated: "Evil spirits emerge only in darkness; once the sun shines, their malign influence dissipates on its own.

sentences.zh: 願一切焚之，以安反側。」

translations.literal: I wish that all be burned, to settle those who are unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that all these documents be burned to reassure those who fear reprisal."

sentences.zh: 周祖從之。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei agreed.

sentences.zh: 師還，遷太常丞。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 從周祖鎮鄴。

translations.literal: He followed the Zhou founder in governing Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Guo Wei when the latter governed Ye.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，授左諫議大夫、樞密直學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed Left Remonstrance Grandee and direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangshun era he was made Left Remonstrance Grandee and direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷中書舍人、翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Secretariat drafter and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became Secretariat drafter and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 三年，加戶部侍郎，改端明殿學士。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the additional title of vice minister of revenue and changed to academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made vice minister of revenue and academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance.

sentences.zh: 周祖疾革，召學士草制，以溥為中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder's illness was critical, he summoned the academician to draft an edict appointing Pu vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Guo Wei summoned an academician to draft an edict making Pu vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 宣制畢，周祖曰：「吾無憂矣。」

translations.literal: When the edict was proclaimed, the Zhou founder said, "I have no more worries."
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was proclaimed, Guo Wei said, "I have no more worries."

sentences.zh: 即日崩。

translations.literal: That same day he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same day.

sentences.zh: 世宗將親征澤、潞，馮道力諫止，溥獨贊成之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong was about to campaign in person against Ze and Lu; Feng Dao strongly remonstrated to stop it, but Pu alone approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong prepared to campaign in person against Ze and Lu, Feng Dao strongly opposed the plan, but Pu alone supported it.

sentences.zh: 凱還，加兼禮部尚書，監修國史。

translations.literal: Returning in triumph, he was given the additional concurrent posts of Minister of Rites and supervisor of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: On his triumphant return he was also made Minister of Rites and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗從容問溥曰：「漢相李崧以蠟書與契丹，猶有記其詞者，信有之耶？」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong once unhurriedly asked Pu, "The Han chief minister Li Song sent a wax-sealed letter to the Khitans, and there are still records of its wording—is it really so?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizong once asked Pu casually, "They say Later Han chief minister Li Song sent a wax-sealed letter to the Khitans, and its wording is still recorded—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 溥曰：「崧為大臣，設有此謀，肯輕示外人？

translations.literal: Pu said, "Song was a great minister; supposing he had such a plot, would he lightly show it to outsiders?
translations.idiomatic: Pu replied, "Song was a great minister. Even if he had such a plot, would he have shown it lightly to outsiders?

sentences.zh: 蓋蘇逢吉誣之耳。」

translations.literal: It was surely Su Fengji who slandered him."
translations.idiomatic: Surely this was slander by Su Fengji."

sentences.zh: 世宗始悟，詔贈其官。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong then understood and issued an edict posthumously restoring his office.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong understood at last and issued an edict restoring Song's posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 世宗將討秦、鳳，求帥於溥，溥薦向拱。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong was about to campaign against Qin and Feng, he sought a commander from Pu; Pu recommended Xiang Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong prepared to campaign against Qin and Feng, he asked Pu to recommend a commander. Pu recommended Xiang Gong.

sentences.zh: 事平，世宗因宴酌酒賜溥曰：「為吾擇帥成邊功者，卿也。」

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Emperor Shizong at a banquet poured wine and bestowed it on Pu, saying, "The one who chose a commander for me and achieved frontier merit is you."
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign succeeded, Shizong raised a cup at a banquet and told Pu, "You are the one who chose the commander who won this frontier victory for me."

sentences.zh: 從平壽春，制加階爵。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Shouchun, an edict added rank and noble title.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Shouchun his rank and noble title were increased.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年，丁外艱。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In 957 he entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 起復，表四上，乞終喪，世宗大怒，宰相范質奏解之，溥懼入謝。

translations.literal: He was recalled from mourning; he submitted four memorials requesting to complete the mourning period. Emperor Shizong was greatly angry; Chief Minister Fan Zhi memorialized to explain it, and Pu in fear entered to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he submitted four memorials asking to complete his filial obligations. Shizong was furious until Fan Zhi intervened; Pu entered court in fear to apologize.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，命參知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year he was ordered to participate in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year he was made a participant in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，加右僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded, he was given the additional title of Right Vice Director of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Pu was made Right Vice Director of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是冬，表請修《世宗實錄》，遂奏史館修撰、都官郎中、知制誥扈蒙，右司員外郎、知制誥張淡，左拾遺王格，直史館、左拾遺董淳，同加修纂，從之。

translations.literal: That winter he memorialized requesting to compile the Veritable Records of Shizong, and thereupon memorialized that Hu Meng, historiography compiler, director in the Bureau of Capital Accounts, and drafter of edicts; Zhang Dan, vice director in the Right Office and drafter of edicts; Wang Ge, Left Remembrancer; and Dong Chun, compiler in the Historiography Institute and Left Remembrancer, all be added to the compilation; this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he asked to compile the Veritable Records of Shizong and recommended Hu Meng, Zhang Dan, Wang Ge, and Dong Chun to assist; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 宋初，進位司空，罷參知樞密院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was advanced to Minister of Works and removed from participating in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was promoted to Minister of Works and relieved of his military affairs duties.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，罷為太子太保。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he was removed and made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 964 he was relieved of office and made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 舊制，一品班於臺省之後，太祖因見溥，謂左右曰：「溥舊相，當寵異之。」

translations.literal: By old regulation, first-rank officials ranked after the censorate and secretariat offices; because Taizu saw Pu, he said to those at his side, "Pu is a former chief minister and should be specially honored."
translations.idiomatic: By old custom, first-rank officials stood behind the censorate and secretariat at court. Seeing Pu one day, Taizu told his attendants, "Pu is a former chief minister and deserves special honor."

sentences.zh: 即令分臺省班東西，遂為定制。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered the censorate and secretariat ranks divided east and west, and this became a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the censorate and secretariat ranks divided to east and west, and this became permanent court practice.

sentences.zh: 五年，丁內艱。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was given the additional title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，遷太子太師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he was transferred to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 969 he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 中謝日，太祖顧左右曰：「溥十年作相，三遷一品，福履之盛，近世未見其比。」

translations.literal: On the day of his court thanks, Taizu looked to those at his side and said, "Pu was chief minister for ten years and was three times promoted to first rank; such fullness of fortune and standing has not been seen in recent times to compare with him."
translations.idiomatic: On the day he thanked the throne, Taizu remarked to his attendants, "Pu served ten years as chief minister and was promoted to first rank three times—such good fortune is unmatched in recent memory."

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，封祁國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 七年八月，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the seventh year at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 輟朝二日，贈侍中，謚文獻。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for two days; he was posthumously given the title of Palace Attendant and given the posthumous title Wénxiàn.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for two days. He was posthumously made Palace Attendant with the posthumous title Literary Exemplar.

sentences.zh: 溥性寬厚，美風度，好汲引後進，其所薦至顯位者甚眾。

translations.literal: Pu was generous and magnanimous by nature, had fine bearing, and liked to draw up and recommend younger men; those he recommended who reached conspicuous posts were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was generous by nature, carried himself with grace, and delighted in advancing younger men—many of his protégés rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 頗吝嗇。

translations.literal: He was rather stingy.
translations.idiomatic: He was himself rather stingy.

sentences.zh: 祚頻領牧守，能殖貨，所至有田宅，家累萬金。

translations.literal: Zuo frequently held prefectural governorships, was able to amass goods, and wherever he went had fields and residences; the family accumulated wealth of tens of thousands in gold.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zuo had often served as prefect and was skilled at accumulating wealth, acquiring fields and houses wherever he went until the family fortune reached tens of thousands in gold.

sentences.zh: 溥在相位，祚以宿州防禦使家居，每公卿至，必首謁祚，置酒上壽，溥朝服趨侍左右，坐客不安席，輒引避。

translations.literal: When Pu was in the chief minister's position, Zuo lived at home as defense commissioner of Suzhou; whenever high officials arrived, they always first paid respects to Zuo, set out wine and offered longevity wishes. Pu in court dress hurried to attend at his side; seated guests could not rest easy and would withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: While Pu served as chief minister, his father Zuo lived in retirement as former defense commissioner of Suzhou. Whenever eminent officials visited, they called first on Zuo with wine and birthday wishes. Pu would hurry to wait on him in court dress, and guests, embarrassed, would withdraw.

sentences.zh: 祚曰：「此豚犬爾，勿煩諸君起。」

translations.literal: Zuo said, "This is just a pig or dog—do not trouble you gentlemen to rise."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo would say, "He is only a pig or dog—do not trouble yourselves to rise."

sentences.zh: 溥諷祚求致政，祚意朝廷未之許也，既得請，祚大罵溥曰：「我筋力未衰，汝欲自固名位，而幽囚我。」

translations.literal: Pu indirectly urged Zuo to request retirement from office; Zuo thought the court had not yet granted it. Once the request was granted, Zuo greatly cursed Pu, saying, "My sinews and strength are not yet weakened—you wish to secure your own fame and position and thereby imprison me."
translations.idiomatic: Pu urged his father to retire. Zuo assumed the court would refuse, but once retirement was granted he raged at Pu: "I am not yet infirm—you only want to secure your own position and have shut me away."

sentences.zh: 舉大梃將擊之，親戚勸諭乃止。

translations.literal: He raised a large staff intending to strike him; relatives admonished and persuaded him before he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He seized a heavy staff to strike him and was restrained only when relatives intervened.

sentences.zh: 溥好學，手不釋卷，嘗集蘇冕《會要》及崔弦《續會要》，補其闕漏，為百卷，曰《唐會要》。

translations.literal: Pu loved learning and never put down his scrolls in hand; he once collected Su Mian's Institutional Compendium and Cui Xian's Continued Compendium, supplemented their omissions, and made a hundred scrolls called the Tang Institutional Compendium.
translations.idiomatic: A devoted scholar who never put down his books, Pu gathered Su Mian's Institutional Compendium and Cui Xian's Continued Compendium, filled their gaps, and produced the hundred-scroll Tang Institutional Compendium.

sentences.zh: 又采朱梁至周為三十卷，曰《五代會要》。

translations.literal: He also gathered from Later Liang through Zhou into thirty scrolls called the Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled thirty scrolls covering Later Liang through Zhou under the title Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子貽孫、貽正、貽慶、貽序。

translations.literal: His sons were Yisun, Yizheng, Yiqing, and Yixu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yisun, Yizheng, Yiqing, and Yixu.

sentences.zh: 貽正至國子博士。

translations.literal: Yizheng reached the office of Doctor in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Yizheng rose to Doctor in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 貽慶比部郎中。

translations.literal: Yiqing was director in the Bureau of Reviews.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing became director in the Bureau of Reviews.

sentences.zh: 貽序，景德二年進士，後改名貽矩，至司封員外郎。

translations.literal: Yixu, jinshi in the second year of Jingde, later changed his name to Yiju and reached vice director in the Bureau of Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: Yixu passed the jinshi examination in 1005, later changed his name to Yiju, and rose to vice director in the Bureau of Enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 貽正子克明，尚太宗女鄭國長公主，改名貽永，令與其父同行，見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Yizheng's son Keming married Taizong's daughter, the Princess of Zheng, changed his name to Yiyong, and was ordered to share the same posthumous line with his father; see the Biography of Imperial Affines.
translations.idiomatic: Yizheng's son Keming married Princess Zheng, Taizong's daughter, changed his name to Yiyong, and was granted to share his father's posthumous honors—see the Biography of Imperial Affines.

sentences.zh: 貽孫，字象賢，少隨周祖典商、潁二州，署衙內都指揮使。

translations.literal: Yisun, styled Xiangxian, in youth followed the Zhou founder in governing the two prefectures of Shang and Ying, and was appointed commander-in-chief within the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun, whose style name was Xiangxian, followed Guo Wei in his youth when the latter governed Shang and Ying prefectures and was appointed commander of the inner yamen guard.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，以父在中書，改朝散大夫、著作佐郎。

translations.literal: During Xiande, because his father was in the Secretariat, he was changed to Grandee of Palace Leisure and assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era, because his father served in the Secretariat, he was made Grandee of Palace Leisure and assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷金部員外郎，賜紫，累遷右司郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was transferred to vice director in the Bureau of the Treasury, was granted purple, and was repeatedly promoted to director in the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he became vice director in the Bureau of the Treasury, was granted the purple robe, and rose to director in the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，卒。

translations.literal: During Chunhua he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Chunhua era.

sentences.zh: 太祖平吳、蜀，所獲文史副本分賜大臣。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Wu and Shu, duplicate copies of literary and historical works obtained were distributed and bestowed on great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu conquered Wu and Shu, duplicate literary and historical works from the conquered states were distributed among the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 溥好聚書，至萬餘卷，貽孫遍覽之；

translations.literal: Pu liked to collect books, reaching more than ten thousand scrolls; Yisun read through them all;
translations.idiomatic: Pu collected more than ten thousand scrolls of books, all of which Yisun read;

sentences.zh: 又多藏法書名畫。

translations.literal: and also stored many model calligraphies and famous paintings.
translations.idiomatic: and also owned many masterpieces of calligraphy and painting.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗問趙普，拜禮何以男子跪而婦人否，普問禮官，不能對。

translations.literal: Taizu once asked Zhao Pu why in bowing rites men knelt but women did not; Pu asked the ritual officials, and they could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once asked Zhao Pu why men knelt in bowing rites while women did not. Pu consulted the ritual officials, but none could answer.

sentences.zh: 貽孫曰：「古詩云『長跪問故夫』，是婦人亦跪也。

translations.literal: Yisun said, "The old poem says 'kneeling long to ask the former husband'—thus women also knelt.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun said, "An old poem runs, 'She knelt long to ask her former husband'—so women knelt as well.

sentences.zh: 唐太后朝婦人始拜而不跪。」

translations.literal: In the Tang dynasty, from the Empress Dowager's court onward, women began to bow but not kneel."
translations.idiomatic: From the Tang empress dowager's court onward, women began to bow without kneeling."

sentences.zh: 普問所出，對云：「太和中，有幽州從事張建章著《渤海國記》，備言其事。」

translations.literal: Pu asked the source; he replied, "In the Taihe era there was Zhang Jianzhang, a staff member of Youzhou, who wrote the Record of the Bohai State, fully explaining this matter."
translations.idiomatic: Pu asked for his source. He replied, "In the Taihe era Zhang Jianzhang of Youzhou wrote the Record of the Bohai State, which explains the change in full."

sentences.zh: 普大稱賞之。

translations.literal: Pu greatly praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，右僕射李昉求郡省百官集議舊儀，貽孫具以對，事見《禮志》，時論許其諳練云。

translations.literal: During Duangong, Right Vice Director Li Fang requested that officials of the prefectural and central offices assemble to discuss old rites; Yisun answered in full, and the matter is seen in the Treatise on Rites; contemporary opinion approved his thorough mastery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Duangong era, Li Fang asked the bureaucracy to discuss old court rituals. Yisun answered every question fully; the account appears in the Treatise on Rites, and contemporaries praised his expertise.

sentences.zh: 魏仁浦

translations.literal: Wei Renpu
translations.idiomatic: Wei Renpu

sentences.zh: 魏仁浦，字道濟，衛州汲人。

translations.literal: Wei Renpu, styled Daoji, was a native of Ji in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Renpu, whose style name was Daoji, came from Ji in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼孤貧，母為假黃縑制暑服，仁浦年十三，嘆曰：「為人子不克供養，乃使慈母求貸以衣我，我能安乎！」

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, his mother borrowed yellow silk to make summer clothes; Renpu at thirteen sighed and said, "As a son I cannot provide support, yet I make my loving mother seek loans to clothe me—how can I be at ease!"
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor as a boy, he once saw his mother borrow yellow silk for summer clothes. At thirteen he sighed and said, "I cannot support my mother, yet she must borrow to clothe me—how can I rest easy?"

sentences.zh: 因慷慨泣下，辭母詣洛陽，濟河沉衣中流，誓曰：「不貴達，不復渡此！」

translations.literal: Thereupon, moved and weeping, he took leave of his mother and went to Luoyang; crossing the river he sank his clothes in midstream and swore, "If I do not reach eminence, I shall not cross this again!"
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, he left his mother for Luoyang, cast his borrowed clothes into the river midstream, and swore, "Unless I achieve success, I shall never cross this river again!"

sentences.zh: 晉末，隸樞密院為小史，任職端謹，儕輩不能及。
