translations.literal: At the end of Jin he was attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs as a minor clerk; in office he was correct and careful, and his peers could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Later Jin he entered the Bureau of Military Affairs as a junior clerk, where his diligence surpassed all his peers.

sentences.zh: 契丹入中原，仁浦隨眾北遷。

translations.literal: When the Khitans entered the Central Plains, Renpu followed the multitude north in relocation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans occupied the Central Plains, Renpu was carried north with the displaced population.

sentences.zh: 會契丹主殂於真定，仁浦得脫歸。

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitan ruler died at Zhending; Renpu was able to escape and return.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan ruler died at Zhending, Renpu escaped and made his way home.

sentences.zh: 魏帥杜重威素知仁浦謹厚，善書計，欲留補牙職。

translations.literal: Wei military commissioner Du Chongwei had long known Renpu as careful and honest and skilled in writing and accounts; he wished to keep him to fill a yamen post.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei, military commissioner of Wei, knew Renpu as diligent and skilled in records and wanted to keep him on his staff.

sentences.zh: 仁浦以重威降將，不願事之，遂遁去。

translations.literal: Renpu, because Chongwei was a surrendering general, was unwilling to serve him and thereupon fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Renpu refused to serve a surrendered general and fled.

sentences.zh: 重威遣騎追之不及。

translations.literal: Chongwei sent horsemen in pursuit but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei sent riders after him but failed to catch him.

sentences.zh: 漢祖起太原，次鞏縣，仁浦迎謁道左，即補舊職。

translations.literal: When the Han founder rose at Taiyuan and halted at Gong county, Renpu met and paid respects by the roadside and was immediately restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhiyuan rose at Taiyuan and halted at Gong county, Renpu met him by the road and was restored to his former post at once.

sentences.zh: 時周祖掌樞密，召仁浦問闕下兵數，仁浦悉能記之，手疏六萬人。

translations.literal: At that time the Zhou founder held the Bureau of Military Affairs; he summoned Renpu and asked the number of troops below the passes. Renpu could remember them all and by hand wrote out sixty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei took charge of military affairs, he asked Renpu how many troops were stationed below the passes. Renpu recited the figure from memory and wrote out sixty thousand men by hand.

sentences.zh: 周祖喜曰：「天下事不足憂也。」

translations.literal: The Zhou founder said with pleasure, "Affairs under Heaven are not worth worrying over."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei said with delight, "There is nothing left to worry about under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 遷兵房主事，從周祖鎮鄴。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs and followed the Zhou founder in governing Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs and accompanied Guo Wei to Ye.

sentences.zh: 乾祐末，隱帝用武德使李鄴等謀，誅大臣楊邠、史弘肇等，密詔澶帥李洪義殺騎將王殷，令郭崇害周祖。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianyou, Emperor Yin used Military Virtue Commissioner Li Ye and others in a plot to execute the chief ministers Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao and others; a secret edict ordered Chun military commissioner Li Hongyi to kill cavalry general Wang Yin and directed Guo Chong to harm the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qianyou, Emperor Yin plotted with Military Virtue Commissioner Li Ye and others to execute chief ministers Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao. A secret edict ordered Chun commissioner Li Hongyi to kill cavalry general Wang Yin and directed Guo Chong to kill Guo Wei.

sentences.zh: 洪義知事不濟，與殷謀，遣副使陳光穗賫詔示周祖。

translations.literal: Hongyi knew the affair would not succeed; conspiring with Yin, he sent Vice Commissioner Chen Guangsu bearing the edict to show the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi knew the plot would fail. Conspiring with Yin, he sent Vice Commissioner Chen Guangsu to show the edict to Guo Wei.

sentences.zh: 周祖懼，召仁浦入計，且示以詔曰：「朝廷將殺我，我死不懼，獨不念麾下將士乎？」

translations.literal: The Zhou founder was afraid; he summoned Renpu to plan and showed him the edict, saying, "The court is about to kill me. I do not fear death, but do they give no thought to the officers and soldiers under my command?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei was alarmed and summoned Renpu for counsel, showing him the edict. He said, "The court means to kill me. I do not fear death, but what of the officers and soldiers under my command?"

sentences.zh: 仁浦曰：「侍中握強兵臨重鎮，有功朝廷，君上信讒，圖害忠良，雖欲割心自明，奚可得也，事將奈何。

translations.literal: Renpu said, "The Palace Attendant holds strong troops facing a great command, has merit to the court, yet the sovereign believes slander and plots harm to the loyal and good. Even if you wished to cut out your heart to prove yourself, how could that be achieved—and what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Renpu said, "You hold strong troops in a key command and have served the court well, yet the emperor believes slander and plots against the loyal. Even cutting out your heart would not clear you. What is to be done?

sentences.zh: 今詔始下，外無知者，莫若易詔以盡誅將士為名，激其怒心，非徒自免，亦可為楊、史雪冤。」

translations.literal: The edict has only just been issued and no one outside knows of it. Better to alter the edict in the name of executing all the officers and soldiers, rouse their angry hearts, and thereby not only save yourself but also clear the wrong done to Yang and Shi."
translations.idiomatic: The edict has only just arrived and no one outside knows of it. Better alter it to order the execution of all your officers and soldiers. That will rouse their anger, save you, and avenge Yang and Shi."

sentences.zh: 周祖納其言，倒用留守印，易詔書以示諸將。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder accepted his words, reversed the use of the garrison seal, altered the edict, and showed it to the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei followed this advice, reversed the garrison seal, altered the edict, and showed it to his generals.

sentences.zh: 眾懼且怒，遂長驅渡河。

translations.literal: The multitude were afraid and angry, and thereupon drove straight across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were frightened and furious and marched straight across the river.

sentences.zh: 及即位，以仁浦為樞密副承旨，俄遷右羽林將軍，充承旨。

translations.literal: When he acceded, Renpu was made deputy privy council receptionist; soon he was transferred to General of the Right Forest Guard and filled the receptionist post.
translations.idiomatic: On accession he made Renpu deputy privy council receptionist, then soon promoted him to General of the Right Forest Guard while keeping him as receptionist.

sentences.zh: 周祖嘗問仁浦諸州屯兵之數及將校名氏，令檢簿視之。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder once asked Renpu the numbers of garrison troops in the various prefectures and the names of officers, ordering him to check the registers and verify.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei once asked him for the garrison strengths and officer rosters of every prefecture and told him to check the registers.

sentences.zh: 仁浦曰：「臣能記之。」

translations.literal: Renpu said, "Your servant can remember them."
translations.idiomatic: Renpu said, "I can remember them, Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 遂手疏於紙，校簿無差，周祖尤倚重焉。

translations.literal: He thereupon wrote them out by hand on paper; compared with the registers there was no discrepancy, and the Zhou founder especially relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote them out from memory without a single error. Guo Wei relied on him ever more heavily.

sentences.zh: 廣順末，太原劉崇寇晉州，仁浦居母喪，而宅邇宮城，周祖步登寬仁門，密遣小黃門召仁浦計事。

translations.literal: At the end of Guangshun, Liu Chong of Taiyuan raided Jinzhou; Renpu was in mourning for his mother, yet his residence was near the palace city. The Zhou founder walked up the Kuanren Gate, secretly sent a junior eunuch to summon Renpu to plan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Guangshun, Liu Chong of Taiyuan attacked Jinzhou. Though in mourning for his mother, Renpu lived near the palace. Guo Wei walked to the Kuanren Gate and secretly sent a eunuch to summon him for counsel.

sentences.zh: 明日，起復舊職。

translations.literal: The next day he was recalled from mourning to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was recalled from mourning to his former duties.

sentences.zh: 周祖大漸，謂世宗曰：「李洪義長與節鎮，魏仁浦無遣違禁密。」

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder was critically ill, he told Emperor Shizong, "Li Hongyi has long been with military commissioners; Wei Renpu has never violated or leaked secrets."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Guo Wei told Shizong, "Li Hongyi has long served with military commissioners; Wei Renpu has never violated or leaked a secret."

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，授右監門衛大將軍、樞密副使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, [Renpu] was appointed Grand General of the Right Gate Guard and Deputy Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Renpu was appointed Grand General of the Right Gate Guard and deputy military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從征高平，周師不利，東偏已潰，仁浦勸世宗出陣西殊死戰，遂克之。

translations.literal: On the campaign at Gaoping the Zhou army fared badly and the eastern wing had already collapsed; Renpu urged Emperor Shizong to go out to the front in the west and fight to the death, and they thereupon prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: On the Gaoping campaign the Zhou army fared badly and the eastern wing collapsed. Renpu urged Shizong to take the field in the west and fight to the death, and they won.

sentences.zh: 師還，拜檢校太保、樞密使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed Honorary Grand Guardian and Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was made Honorary Grand Guardian and military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 故事，惟宰相生辰賜器幣鞍馬，世宗特以賜仁浦。

translations.literal: By precedent only chief ministers on their birthdays were granted vessels, silks, saddles, and horses; Emperor Shizong specially granted these to Renpu.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent only chief ministers received vessels, silks, saddles, and horses on their birthdays, but Shizong specially granted them to Renpu.

sentences.zh: 從平壽春，加檢校太傅，進爵邑，遷中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士兼樞密使。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Shouchun, he was given the additional title of Honorary Grand Tutor, advanced in noble rank and fief, and transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with concurrent appointment as Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouchun was pacified he was made Honorary Grand Tutor, advanced in rank and fief, and appointed vice director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 世宗欲命仁浦為相，議者以其不由科第，世宗曰：「古人為宰相者，豈盡由科第耶？」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong wished to appoint Renpu chief minister; critics said he had not come through the civil service examination. Emperor Shizong said, "Of those who served as chief ministers in antiquity, were they all produced by the examination?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizong wished to make Renpu chief minister, but critics objected that he had not passed the civil service examination. Shizong said, "Did all ancient chief ministers come through the examination?"

sentences.zh: 遂決意用之。

translations.literal: He thereupon resolved to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: He then resolved to appoint him.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，加刑部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded, [Renpu] was given the additional title of Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Renpu was additionally made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 宋初，進位右僕射，以疾在告。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was advanced to Right Vice Director of State Affairs and was on sick leave reporting illness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was promoted to Right Vice Director of State Affairs but was on sick leave.

sentences.zh: 太祖幸其第，賜黃金器二百兩、錢二百萬。

translations.literal: Taizu visited his residence and bestowed two hundred taels of gold vessels and two million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu visited his home and gave him two hundred taels of gold vessels and two million cash.

sentences.zh: 再上表乞骸骨，不許。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial requesting to retire on account of old bones; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to retire, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，罷守本官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he was removed while retaining his nominal office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiande era he was relieved of active duty while keeping his title.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，春宴，太祖笑謂仁浦曰：「何不勸我一杯酒？」

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, at a spring banquet, Taizu smilingly said to Renpu, "Why do you not urge me to drink a cup of wine?"
translations.idiomatic: At a spring banquet in 969, Taizu smiled and said to Renpu, "Why don't you urge me to take a drink?"

sentences.zh: 仁浦奉觴上壽，帝密謂之曰：「朕欲親征太原，如何？」

translations.literal: Renpu raised the goblet and offered longevity wishes; the emperor secretly said to him, "I wish to campaign in person against Taiyuan—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Renpu raised his cup and offered a toast. The emperor whispered, "I mean to campaign against Taiyuan in person—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 仁浦曰：「欲速不達，惟陛下慎之。」

translations.literal: Renpu said, "Haste makes no progress; may Your Majesty be cautious."
translations.idiomatic: Renpu replied, "Haste defeats its own purpose—Your Majesty should proceed with caution."

sentences.zh: 宴罷，就第，復賜上尊酒十石、御膳羊百口。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended, he went to his residence and was again bestowed ten piculs of imperial wine and a hundred imperial banquet sheep.
translations.idiomatic: After the banquet he returned home to further gifts of ten piculs of imperial wine and a hundred imperial sheep.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，中途遇疾。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Taiyuan, he fell ill midway.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the Taiyuan campaign but fell ill on the march.

sentences.zh: 還，至梁侯驛卒，年五十九，贈侍中。

translations.literal: On the return he died at Lianghou Post Station, aged fifty-nine; he was posthumously given the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey he died at Lianghou Post Station at the age of fifty-nine and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 仁浦性寬厚，接士大夫有禮，務以德報怨。

translations.literal: Renpu was generous and magnanimous by nature, received scholar-officials with courtesy, and strove to repay enmity with virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Renpu was generous by nature, courteous to scholar-officials, and determined to repay injury with kindness.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，有鄭元昭者，開封浚儀人，為安邑、解縣兩池榷鹽使，遷解州刺史。

translations.literal: During Qianyou of Han there was Zheng Yuanzhao, a man of Junyi in Kaifeng, who was salt monopoly commissioner of the two pools of Anyi and Jie county, and was transferred to prefect of Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou era there was Zheng Yuanzhao of Junyi in Kaifeng, salt monopoly commissioner for the Anyi and Jie pools, later prefect of Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 會詔以仁浦婦翁李溫玉為榷鹽使管兩池，元昭不得專其利。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict appointed Renpu's father-in-law Li Wenyu as salt monopoly commissioner to manage the two pools, and Yuanzhao could not monopolize the profits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then appointed Renpu's father-in-law Li Wenyu to manage both salt pools, depriving Yuanzhao of his monopoly profits.

sentences.zh: 仁浦方為樞密院主事，元昭意仁浦必庇溫玉，會李守貞以河中叛，溫玉子在城中，元昭即繫溫玉以變聞。

translations.literal: Renpu was then chief clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs; Yuanzhao thought Renpu would surely shield Wenyu. It happened that Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and Wenyu's son was in the city; Yuanzhao immediately detained Wenyu and reported a mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Renpu was then chief clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs. Yuanzhao assumed he would protect Wenyu. When Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and Wenyu's son was trapped in the city, Yuanzhao arrested Wenyu and reported a conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 時周祖總樞務，知其有間，置而不問。

translations.literal: At that time the Zhou founder oversaw military affairs, knew there was a private grudge involved, and set it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei, then in charge of military affairs, saw the private grudge involved and took no action.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，仁浦為樞密使，元昭不自安。

translations.literal: During Xiande, Renpu was military affairs commissioner; Yuanzhao was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Renpu became military affairs commissioner in the Xiande era, Yuanzhao grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 及代歸闕，道洛都，以情告仁浦弟仁滌，仁滌曰：「公第去，可無憂。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned to court, passing through Luoyang, he confided his feelings to Renpu's younger brother Rendi; Rendi said, "When you, sir, leave your post, you may be without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court after his term, he confided his fears to Renpu's brother Rendi in Luoyang. Rendi said, "Once you leave your post, you need not worry.

sentences.zh: 我兄素寬仁有度，雖公事不欲傷於人，豈念私隙乎？」

translations.literal: My elder brother has always been generous and measured; though in public affairs he does not wish to harm people, would he bear private grudges in mind?"
translations.idiomatic: My brother has always been magnanimous. He avoids harming others even in public affairs—why would he harbor a private grudge?"

sentences.zh: 元昭至京師，仁浦果不介意，白周祖授元昭慶州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yuanzhao reached the capital, Renpu truly took no offense and reported to the Zhou founder to appoint Yuanzhao prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanzhao reached the capital, Renpu showed no resentment and recommended him to the Zhou founder for appointment as prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 漢隱帝寵作坊使賈延徽，延徽與仁浦並居，欲倂其第，屢譖仁浦，幾至不測。

translations.literal: Emperor Yin of Han favored the workshop commissioner Jia Yanhui; Yanhui lived next to Renpu and wished to annex his residence, repeatedly slandering Renpu until he nearly reached unforeseen disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yin favored the workshop commissioner Jia Yanhui, who lived beside Renpu and sought to seize his house. Yanhui slandered Renpu repeatedly and nearly brought him to ruin.

sentences.zh: 及周祖入汴，有擒延徽授仁浦者，仁浦謝曰：「因兵戈以報怨，不忍為也。」

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder entered Bian, some captured Yanhui and handed him to Renpu; Renpu declined, saying, "To repay a grudge by means of arms—I cannot bear to do that."
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei entered Bian, some captured Yanhui and offered him to Renpu. Renpu refused, saying, "I cannot repay a grudge with violence."

sentences.zh: 力保全之。

translations.literal: He exerted himself to preserve and protect him completely.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he worked to protect him.

sentences.zh: 當時稱其長者。

translations.literal: At the time he was praised as an elder of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised him as a man of true magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 世宗朝，近侍有忤上至死者，仁浦力救之，全活者眾。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizong's court, when close attendants offended the sovereign to the point of death, Renpu strove to save them, and those wholly preserved alive were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong, when attendants who offended the emperor faced execution, Renpu often intervened and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 淮南之役，獲賊數千人，仁浦從容上言，俾隸諸軍，軍中無濫殺者。

translations.literal: In the Huainan campaign, several thousand bandits were captured; Renpu unhurriedly memorialized that they be assigned to the various armies, and in the army there were none indiscriminately killed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huainan campaign, thousands of captives were taken. Renpu calmly memorialized that they be assigned to army units, and no indiscriminate killings followed.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，其子咸信請謚曰宣懿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde, his son Xianxin requested the posthumous title Xuan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1007 his son Xianxin petitioned for the posthumous title Magnanimous and Cultivated.

sentences.zh: 子咸美、咸熙、咸信。

translations.literal: His sons were Xianmei, Xianxi, and Xianxin.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xianmei, Xianxi, and Xianxin.

sentences.zh: 咸美以左司禦率府率致仕。

translations.literal: Xianmei retired as commandant of the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard Command.
translations.idiomatic: Xianmei retired as commandant of the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard Command.

sentences.zh: 咸熙性仁孝，嘗會賓客，家童數輩覆案碎器，客皆驚愕，咸熙色不變，止令更設饌具，其寬厚若此，以父任，累遷屯田郎中，後至太僕少卿，卒年四十九。

translations.literal: Xianxi was benevolent and filial by nature; once when entertaining guests, several household boys overturned the table and broke vessels; the guests were all startled, but Xianxi's expression did not change—he only ordered the feast set out again. His generosity was like this. By his father's privilege he was repeatedly promoted to director in the Bureau of State Farms, later reaching Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, and died aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxi was gentle and filial. Once, while entertaining guests, servants overturned a table and smashed the dishes. The guests were startled, but Xianxi showed no dismay and simply ordered a fresh setting. Such was his forbearance. Through his father's privilege he rose to director in the Bureau of State Farms and eventually Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud; he died at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子昭慶，駕部員外郎；

translations.literal: His son Zhaoqing was vice director in the Bureau of the Imperial Carriage;
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaoqing became vice director in the Bureau of the Imperial Carriage;

sentences.zh: 昭文，西染院使；

translations.literal: Zhaowen was commissioner of the Western Dyeing Institute;
translations.idiomatic: Zhaowen was commissioner of the Western Dyeing Institute;

sentences.zh: 昭素，供奉官、閣門祗侯。

translations.literal: Zhaosu was a tribute officer and palace gate usher.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaosu was a tribute officer and palace gate usher.

sentences.zh: 子 咸信

translations.literal: Son: Xianxin
translations.idiomatic: Son: Xianxin

sentences.zh: 咸信，字國寶，建隆初，授朝散大夫、太子右坊通事舍人，改供奉官。

translations.literal: Xianxin, styled Guobao, at the beginning of Jianlong was appointed Grandee of Palace Leisure and Communications Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Right Quarters, then changed to tribute officer.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxin, whose style name was Guobao, was made Grandee of Palace Leisure and communications attendant to the heir apparent early in the Jianlong era, then tribute officer.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖在潛邸，昭憲太后嘗至仁浦第，咸信方幼，侍母側，儼如成人。

translations.literal: At first, when Taizu was in his hidden residence, Empress Dowager Zhaoxian once came to Renpu's residence; Xianxin was still young, attending at his mother's side with the bearing of an adult.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizu was still heir apparent, Empress Dowager Zhaoxian visited Renpu's home and found the young Xianxin standing dutifully at his mother's side with the composure of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 太后奇之，欲結姻好。

translations.literal: The empress dowager marveled at him and wished to form a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was impressed and wished to arrange a marriage.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，太宗尹京，成昭憲之意，延見咸信於便殿，命與御帶党進等較射，稱善。

translations.literal: During Kaibao, Taizong governed the capital, fulfilling the empress dowager's wish; he received Xianxin in audience in the side hall, ordered him to compete in archery with the imperial guard Dang Jin and others, and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era Taizong governed the capital and carried out the empress dowager's wish. He received Xianxin in the side hall, had him compete in archery with the imperial guard Dang Jin and others, and praised his skill.

sentences.zh: 遂選尚永慶公主，授右衛將軍、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He was then selected to marry Princess Yongqing and was appointed General of the Right Guard and Commandant Escorting the Imperial Son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: He was then chosen to marry Princess Yongqing and was made General of the Right Guard and imperial son-in-law commandant.

sentences.zh: 逾年，出領吉州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he went out to head Jizhou as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，真拜本州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was truly appointed defense commissioner of his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he was formally appointed defense commissioner of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔用奉外賜錢十萬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict granted him one hundred thousand in cash beyond his salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year an edict granted him one hundred thousand cash beyond his salary.

sentences.zh: 五年，坐遣親吏市木西邊，矯制免所過稅算，罰一季奉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was punished for sending a personal clerk to purchase timber on the western frontier and falsely issuing orders to exempt transit taxes and levies; one season's salary was fined.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was fined one season's salary for sending a personal clerk to buy timber on the western frontier and falsely exempting transit taxes.

sentences.zh: 俄遷慎州觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to observation commissioner of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made observation commissioner of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年冬，契丹擾邊，王師出討，悉命諸主婿鎮要地：王承衍知大名，石保吉知河陽，咸信知澶州。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Yongxi the Khitans disturbed the frontier and the royal army went out to campaign; all the imperial sons-in-law were ordered to guard key places: Wang Chengyan governed Daming, Shi Baoji governed Heyang, and Xianxin governed Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 986, when the Khitans raided the border, the court ordered its sons-in-law to guard key posts: Wang Chengyan at Daming, Shi Baoji at Heyang, and Xianxin at Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，本郡黃河清，咸信以聞，詔褒答之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Yellow River ran clear in his command; Xianxin reported it, and an edict praised and answered him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Yellow River ran clear in his jurisdiction. Xianxin reported the omen and received an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 籍田畢，就拜彰德軍節度。

translations.literal: When the plowing ceremony was completed, he was immediately appointed military commissioner of the Zhangde army.
translations.idiomatic: After the plowing ceremony he was appointed military commissioner of the Zhangde army.

sentences.zh: 八月，遣歸治所。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was sent back to his administrative seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was sent back to his command.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，河決澶淵，陷北城，再命知州事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua the river burst at Chunyuan and submerged the north city; he was again ordered to govern the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 993 the Yellow River burst at Chunyuan and flooded the north city. Xianxin was again put in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太宗親諭方略，傳置而往。

translations.literal: Taizong personally instructed him on strategy, and he went by relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong personally briefed him on strategy, and he traveled by relay post.

sentences.zh: 時遣閻承翰修河橋，咸信請及流水未下造舟為便，承翰入奏：「方冬難成，請權罷其役。」

translations.literal: At that time Yan Chenghan was sent to repair the river bridge; Xianxin requested that boats be built before the current came down, which would be convenient. Chenghan entered and memorialized, "It is hard to complete in midwinter—please temporarily halt the labor."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Chenghan had been sent to repair the river bridge. Xianxin urged building boats before the spring flood. Chenghan memorialized, "It is hard to complete in midwinter—please temporarily halt the labor."

sentences.zh: 咸信因其去，乃集工成之。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of his departure, Xianxin thereupon gathered workers and completed it.
translations.idiomatic: After Chenghan left, Xianxin gathered workers and finished the boats himself.

sentences.zh: 奏至，上大悅。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 河平，遣還役兵，俄詔留築堤，咸信以為天寒地涸，無決溢之患，復奏罷之。

translations.literal: When the river was pacified, the labor troops were sent back; soon an edict ordered them retained to build dikes. Xianxin thought that with cold weather and dry ground there was no danger of breach and overflow, and again memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: After the river subsided the laborers were dismissed, but soon an edict ordered them kept to build dikes. Xianxin argued that in the cold, dry season there was no risk of breach and memorialized to stop the work.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，改定國軍節度。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong acceded, [Xianxin] was transferred to the Dingguo army commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong acceded, Xianxin was transferred to the Dingguo army commission.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，大閱東郊，以為舊城內都巡檢。

translations.literal: During Xianping, at the great review in the eastern suburbs, he was made metropolitan patrol inspector within the old city.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era, at the great review in the eastern suburbs, he was made metropolitan patrol inspector within the old city.

sentences.zh: 車駕北征，為貝冀路行營都統署，詔督師。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned north, he served as overall supervisor of the Beiji route mobile headquarters and was ordered by edict to direct the army.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern campaign he served as overall supervisor of the Beiji route mobile headquarters and was ordered to direct the army.

sentences.zh: 至貝州，敵人退，召還行在所。

translations.literal: When he reached Beizhou the enemy withdrew, and he was recalled to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: At Beizhou the enemy withdrew and he was recalled to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 景德初，從幸澶州，石保吉與李繼隆為排陣使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he followed in attendance at Chunzhou; Shi Baoji and Li Jilong served as array marshals.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era he accompanied the court to Chunzhou, where Shi Baoji and Li Jilong served as array marshals.

sentences.zh: 契丹請和，帝置酒行宮，面賞繼隆、保吉，咸信避席，自愧無功，上笑而撫慰之。

translations.literal: The Khitans sought peace; the emperor set out wine in the traveling palace and rewarded Jilong and Baoji to their faces. Xianxin left his seat, ashamed at having no merit; the sovereign smiled and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans sued for peace the emperor held a banquet in the traveling palace and rewarded Jilong and Baoji in person. Xianxin rose from his seat, ashamed of having achieved nothing, and the emperor smiled and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 二年，改武成軍節度，知曹州。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to the Wucheng army commission and governed Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made military commissioner of the Wucheng army and prefect of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 秋霖積潦，咸信決廣濟河堤以導之，民田無害。

translations.literal: Autumn rains piled up floodwater; Xianxin breached the Guangji River dike to channel it away, and the people's fields suffered no harm.
translations.idiomatic: After autumn rains flooded the fields, Xianxin breached the Guangji River dike to channel the water away and spared the farmland.

sentences.zh: 扈駕朝陵還，上言先墳在洛，欲立碑，求涖盟津，以便其事，即改知河陽。

translations.literal: Returning from escorting the imperial carriage to pay respects at the tombs, he memorialized that his ancestors' graves were in Luoyang and he wished to erect a stele; he asked to govern Mengjin to facilitate the matter, and was thereupon transferred to govern Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from escorting the emperor to the imperial tombs, he reported that his ancestors were buried in Luoyang and asked to erect a stele. He requested appointment at Mengjin to facilitate the work and was transferred to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，從東封，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he followed the eastern feng sacrifice and was given the additional title of Honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu era he accompanied the eastern feng sacrifice and was made Honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 將祀汾陰，命知澶州，令入內副都知張繼能諭旨。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice at Fenyin was to be performed, he was ordered to govern Chunzhou, and Palace Deputy Capital Gate Director Zhang Jineng was ordered to convey the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Fenyin sacrifice he was put in charge of Chunzhou, and Palace Deputy Capital Gate Director Zhang Jineng was sent to convey the imperial instructions.

sentences.zh: 移領忠武軍節度。

translations.literal: He was transferred to head the Zhongwu army commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to the Zhongwu army commission.

sentences.zh: 未幾召還，年已昏眊，見上，希旨求寵渥。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled; his years had already dimmed his sight. On seeing the sovereign he sought favor by pleasing his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon recalled to court, he was by then dim-sighted and sought further favor from the emperor.

sentences.zh: 七年，表乞任用，上出示中書向敏中曰：「咸信聯榮戚里，位居節制，復何望耶？」

translations.literal: In the seventh year he memorialized requesting employment; the emperor showed it to Chief Minister Xiang Minzhong and said, "Xianxin is linked in glory with the imperial kin, holds a military commissioner's post—what more does he hope for?"
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he petitioned for a new appointment. The emperor showed the memorial to Xiang Minzhong and said, "Xianxin is already an imperial in-law and a military commissioner—what more does he want?"

sentences.zh: 是冬，以新建南京，獎太祖舊臣，加同平章事。

translations.literal: That winter, because the Southern Capital was newly built, to reward Taizu's old ministers he was given the additional title of Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, to reward Taizu's old followers on the establishment of the Southern Capital, he was made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 俄判天雄軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made administrator of the Tianxiong army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made administrator of the Tianxiong army.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，改陜州大都督府長史、保平軍節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi he was changed to chief administrator of the great protectorate prefecture of Shaanzhou and military commissioner of the Baoping army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianxi era he was made chief administrator of Shaanzhou and military commissioner of the Baoping army.

sentences.zh: 有感風疾苦，歸。

translations.literal: He suffered from wind ailment and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Afflicted by rheumatism, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗謂宰相曰：「咸信老病，諸子不克承順，身後復能保守其家業耶？」

translations.literal: Zhenzong once said to the chief ministers, "Xianxin is old and ill; his sons cannot succeed in obedience—after his death can they still preserve the family estate?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong once asked his chief ministers, "Xianxin is old and ill, and his sons are undutiful—can they preserve the family fortune after his death?"

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年六十九，贈中書令。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-nine; he was posthumously given the title of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward at sixty-nine and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 錄其諸子孫侄，遷官者七人。

translations.literal: His various sons, grandsons, and nephews were enrolled; seven received promotions in office.
translations.idiomatic: Seven of his sons, grandsons, and nephews were enrolled and promoted in office.

sentences.zh: 咸信頗知書，善待士，然性吝喜利，仁浦所營邸舍悉擅有之。

translations.literal: Xianxin was rather learned in books and treated scholars well, yet by nature he was stingy and fond of profit; all the lodging houses Renpu had built he appropriated for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxin was literate and courteous to scholars, but stingy and greedy. He seized all the lodging houses his father Renpu had built.

sentences.zh: 既卒，為諸侄所訟，時人恥之。

translations.literal: After he died he was sued by his various nephews, and people of the time were shamed by it.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his nephews sued over the property, to the shame of contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 子昭易、昭亮、昭侃。

translations.literal: His sons were Zhaoyi, Zhaoliang, and Zhaokan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhaoyi, Zhaoliang, and Zhaokan.

sentences.zh: 昭易，西京作坊使，知隰州；

translations.literal: Zhaoyi was commissioner of the Western Capital workshop and governed Xizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi was commissioner of the Western Capital workshop and prefect of Xizhou;

sentences.zh: 昭侃，改名昭昺，為崇儀使。

translations.literal: Zhaokan changed his name to Zhaobing and was made commissioner of the Honored Ceremonial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaokan changed his name to Zhaobing and became commissioner of the Honored Ceremonial Guard.

sentences.zh: 孫 昭亮

translations.literal: Grandson: Zhaoliang
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Zhaoliang

sentences.zh: 昭亮，字克明，公主所生。

translations.literal: Zhaoliang, styled Keming, was born of the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoliang, whose style name was Keming, was the princess's son.

sentences.zh: 幼未名，太宗召入禁中，命賦賞花詩，詩成上之，太宗大悅，酌以上尊酒，命筆題「從訓」、「昭亮」二名，令自擇之。

translations.literal: Young and not yet named, Taizong summoned him into the inner palace, ordered him to compose a poem on viewing flowers; when the poem was completed and submitted, Taizong was greatly pleased, poured him imperial wine, and ordered a brush to inscribe the two names "Congxun" and "Zhaoliang," letting him choose for himself.
translations.idiomatic: As a child without a given name, he was summoned to the inner palace by Taizong and told to compose a poem on flowers. Taizong was delighted, offered him imperial wine, and wrote two names—"Congxun" and "Zhaoliang"—for him to choose.

sentences.zh: 拜如京副使，遷如京、洛苑使，掌翰林司。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice commissioner of the Capital Reception Office, transferred to commissioner of the Capital and Luoyang parklands, and managed the Hanlin office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice commissioner of the Capital Reception Office, then commissioner of the capital and Luoyang parklands, with charge of the Hanlin office.

sentences.zh: 丁公主憂，起復，授六宅使，領富州刺史，遷內藏庫副使，未幾，拜西上閣門使，進秩東上。

translations.literal: On entering mourning for the princess he was recalled from mourning, appointed commissioner of the Six Residences, concurrently held Fuzhou prefect, was transferred to vice commissioner of the Inner Treasury, and before long was made western upper palace gate commissioner and advanced in rank to eastern upper.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for the princess he was recalled to service, made commissioner of the Six Residences and prefect of Fuzhou, then vice commissioner of the Inner Treasury. Soon he became western upper palace gate commissioner and was promoted to eastern upper.

sentences.zh: 上言閣門舊儀制未當，乃詔龍圖閣學士陳彭年、待制張知白、引進使白文肇與昭亮同加詳定，既成，賜白金千兩。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the old regulations of the palace gates were improper; an edict then ordered Hanlin academician Chen Pengnian, drafting academician Zhang Zhibai, introduction commissioner Bai Wenzhao, and Zhaoliang together to add detailed revision. When it was completed, one thousand taels of white gold were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that palace gate protocol was outdated. The court ordered Chen Pengnian, Zhang Zhibai, Bai Wenzhao, and Zhaoliang to revise it. On completion he received one thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 又建議設儀石於內殿，加領恩州團練使。

translations.literal: He also proposed setting ceremonial stones in the inner hall and was given the additional concurrent post of training commissioner of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed installing ceremonial stones in the inner hall and was made training commissioner of Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 時咸信在大名，屬生日，命昭亮就賜禮物。

translations.literal: At that time Xianxin was at Daming; on the occasion of his birthday, Zhaoliang was ordered to go and bestow gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianxin was at Daming, the court sent Zhaoliang to deliver birthday gifts on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 是日，告命至，軍府榮之。

translations.literal: That day the commission arrived, and the military headquarters honored the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: That day the commission arrived, and the military headquarters celebrated the honor.

sentences.zh: 父卒，遷四方館使，仍兼掌客省，多糾群官之失儀者。

translations.literal: When his father died he was transferred to commissioner of the Four Directions Hall, still concurrently managing the Bureau of Receiving Guests, and often corrected officials who breached ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he became commissioner of the Four Directions Hall while still managing the Bureau of Receiving Guests, and frequently disciplined officials for breaches of court etiquette.

sentences.zh: 昭亮多病在告，詔給其奉。

translations.literal: Zhaoliang was often ill and on sick leave; an edict granted him his salary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoliang was often ill on leave; the court continued his salary by edict.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Tianxi era.

sentences.zh: 昭亮未死日，數遣人入謁，求進用，加兼端州防禦使。

translations.literal: Before Zhaoliang died he repeatedly sent people to request audience, seeking advancement in employment, and was given the additional concurrent post of defense commissioner of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before his death Zhaoliang repeatedly petitioned for promotion and was made defense commissioner of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 未及拜命，死，仍以制書賜其家，贈貝州觀察使。

translations.literal: Before he could receive the commission he died; an edict was still bestowed on his family, and he was posthumously given the title of observation commissioner of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died before he could take up the post, but the court still issued the commission to his family and posthumously made him observation commissioner of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 以弟昭侃為供備庫使，子餘慶為內殿崇班。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhaokan was made commissioner of the Supply and Equipment Storehouse, and his son Yuqing was made inner-palace honored guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhaokan was made commissioner of the Supply and Equipment Storehouse, and his son Yuqing was made an inner-palace honored guardsman.

sentences.zh: 昭亮與陳彭年款昵，彭年嘗稱其才。

translations.literal: Zhaoliang was on intimate terms with Chen Pengnian, and Pengnian once praised his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoliang was on close terms with Chen Pengnian, who once praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 昭亮居官務察，多遣人偵伺僚輩，樞密承旨尹德潤嘗少之。

translations.literal: In office Zhaoliang strove to investigate closely, often sending people to spy on his colleagues; the military affairs drafter Yin Derun once looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: In office Zhaoliang was obsessively watchful, often sending agents to spy on colleagues. Yin Derun, drafter in the Bureau of Military Affairs, despised him.

sentences.zh: 會閣門副使焦守節、內殿崇班郭盛以役卒與德潤治第，昭亮廉知，發其事，皆坐黜削。

translations.literal: It happened that Vice Commissioner of the Palace Gates Jiao Shoujie and inner-palace honored guardsman Guo Sheng used corvée laborers to build a residence for Derun; Zhaoliang learned of it through investigation and exposed the affair; all were punished with dismissal and reduction.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Commissioner Jiao Shoujie and honored guardsman Guo Sheng used corvée laborers to build a house for Derun, Zhaoliang uncovered the affair and had them all dismissed and demoted.

sentences.zh: 李維，即王曾妻子叔父，同在翰林，曾受詔試舉人，以家事屬維。

translations.literal: Li Wei was the wife's uncle of Wang Zeng; both were in the Hanlin Academy. Zeng received an edict to examine candidates and entrusted family affairs to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei was the uncle of Wang Zeng's wife. Both served in the Hanlin Academy. When Zeng was ordered to examine candidates, he asked Wei to handle a family matter.

sentences.zh: 昭亮意曾受祈請，奏其竊語。

translations.literal: Zhaoliang supposed Zeng had received a private request and memorialized about their whispered conversation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoliang assumed Zeng had accepted a private favor and memorialized accusing him of improper conversation.

sentences.zh: 遣中使參問，無他狀，曾始得釋。

translations.literal: An imperial envoy was sent to investigate; there was no other circumstance, and only then was Zeng released.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial envoy investigated and found nothing further; only then was Zeng cleared.

sentences.zh: 昭亮陰險多此類，時人惡之。

translations.literal: Zhaoliang was insidious and treacherous in many matters of this kind, and people of the time detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoliang was treacherous in many such ways, and contemporaries despised him.

sentences.zh: 餘慶，改名成德，為供備庫副使。

translations.literal: Yuqing changed his name to Chengde and was made vice commissioner of the Supply and Equipment Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing changed his name to Chengde and became vice commissioner of the Supply and Equipment Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：五季至周之世宗，天下將定之時也。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: From the Five Dynasties to Emperor Shizong of Zhou was the time when all under Heaven was about to be settled.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser remarks: From the Five Dynasties through Emperor Shizong of Zhou was the age when the empire was nearing its final settlement.

sentences.zh: 范質、王溥、魏仁浦，世宗之所拔擢，而皆有宰相之器焉。

translations.literal: Fan Zhi, Wang Pu, and Wei Renpu were men whom Shizong promoted and selected, and all had the capacity of chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi, Wang Pu, and Wei Renpu were promoted by Shizong, and each had the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 宋祖受命，遂為佐命元臣，天之所置，果非人之所能測歟。

translations.literal: When the Song founder received the Mandate, they thereupon became founding ministers who aided the mandate; what Heaven places—can it truly be what human beings are able to fathom?
translations.idiomatic: When the Song founder received the Mandate, they became his founding ministers—surely Heaven's placement lies beyond human foresight.

sentences.zh: 質以儒者曉暢軍事，及其為相，廉慎守法。

translations.literal: Zhi, as a Confucian scholar, was thoroughly versed in military affairs; when he became chief minister he was incorrupt, cautious, and observed the law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, though a scholar, understood military affairs thoroughly; as chief minister he was incorrupt, cautious, and scrupulous in observing the law.

sentences.zh: 溥刀筆家子，而好學終始不倦。

translations.literal: Pu was the son of a clerk's family, yet he loved learning from beginning to end without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Pu came from a clerk's family, yet he loved learning without cease from youth to old age.

sentences.zh: 仁浦嘗為小史，而與溥皆以寬厚長者著稱，豈非絕人之資乎。

translations.literal: Renpu had once been a minor clerk, yet he and Pu were both famed as generous and elder-like men of virtue—is this not talent that surpasses ordinary men?
translations.idiomatic: Renpu had once been a junior clerk, yet he and Pu were both renowned for magnanimity—were these not gifts that set them apart from ordinary men?

sentences.zh: 質臨終，戒其後勿請謚立碑，自悔深矣。

translations.literal: At his end Zhi admonished his descendants not to request a posthumous title or erect a stele; his self-reproach was deep indeed.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Zhi told his heirs not to seek a posthumous title or erect a tomb inscription—his remorse ran very deep.

sentences.zh: 太宗評質惜其欠世宗一死。

translations.literal: Taizong judged Zhi and regretted that he lacked dying once for Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong remarked that Zhi's sole failing was not having died for Shizong.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之法責備賢者，質可得免乎！

translations.literal: By the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals, worthy men are held to strict account—can Zhi be exempted!
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals hold even the worthy to strict account—can Zhi truly be exempted!
